sites.name: Arch of Constantine
sites.address: P.za del Colosseo, 00184 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: Rome's largest triumphal arch, raised for Constantine's victory at the Milvian Bridge.
sites.description: A triumphal arch in Rome dedicated to the emperor Constantine, to commemorate his victory over Maxentius at the Battle of the Milvian Bridge

sites.name: Basilica of Maxentius and Constantine
sites.address: Clivo di Venere Felice, 00186 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: Colossal vaulted basilica in the Forum, begun by Maxentius, finished by Constantine.
sites.description: A civic basilica in the Roman Forum, begun under Maxentius and completed under Constantine, this is absolutely enormous and worth standing in just to get a sense of scale.

sites.name: Column of Phocas
sites.address: Via dei Fori Imperiali, 1, 00186 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: The last monument ever raised in the Roman Forum, honoring a Byzantine emperor.
sites.description: A monumental column in the Roman Forum, built after the reconquest of Rome from the Ostrogoths, and dedicated to Emperor Phocas in 608

sites.name: Colossus of Constantine
sites.address: Via del Campidoglio, 1, 00196 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: Giant fragments of a seated Constantine, now in the Capitoline courtyard.
sites.description: A monumental statue of Constantine I, previously displayed in the Basilica of Constantine and Maxentius, and now in fragments at the Capitoline Museums

sites.name: Mausoleum of Constantina
sites.summary: Constantine's daughter's tomb, ringed by dazzling 4th-century mosaics.
sites.description: A mausoleum built for Emperor Constantine's daughter, containing notable mosaics, dome painting, and sarcophagi

sites.name: San Cesareo in Palatio
sites.address: Via di Porta San Sebastiano, 2, 00153 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: Small ancient church over Roman ruins, cloaked in Baroque decoration.
sites.description: A church dedicated to St. Caesarius of Terracina, whose relics were said to have been moved here. Archaeological evidence suggests the first church was built in the 8th century. Decoration is mostly post-renovation 17th century.

sites.name: Basilica of San Clemente
sites.address: Piazza di S. Clemente, 00184 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: Layered basilica crowned by a golden Byzantine apse mosaic.
sites.description: A church dedicated to Pope St. Clement I, noted for its unique Byzantine arabesque apse dome mosaics

sites.name: San Giovanni a Porta Latina
alternateNames: Saint John Before the Latin Gate
sites.address: Via di Porta Latina, 17, 00179 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: Serene 5th-century church by the Latin Gate honoring St John the Evangelist.
sites.description: A church constructed in the late 5th century and restored in the 8th, commemorating the attempted martyrdom of St. John the Evangelist at the Latin Gate

sites.name: Lateran Baptistery
sites.address: P.za di S. Giovanni in Laterano, 4, 00184 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: The model for Christian baptisteries, with porphyry columns and Milvian Bridge scenes.
sites.description: A baptistery connected to the Archbasilica of Saint John Lateran with porphyry columns and ceiling tiles that tell the story of the Battle of the Milvian Bridge

sites.name: Archbasilica of Saint John Lateran
sites.address: P.za. San Giovanni In Laterano, 00184 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: The pope's own cathedral and mother church of the Catholic world.
sites.description: The seat of the Bishop of Rome, the oldest public church in the city of Rome, and the ecumenical mother church of the Roman Catholic faith. Founded in 324, and extensively updated, mostly in the 16th and 17th centuries. Byzantine history enthusiasts will also note that this is the site of the Lateran Council of 769, denouncing the Byzantine iconoclasts. The apse mosaics are from the 13th century, but the Acheropita icon that sits atop the Scala Santa across the street is mid-5th century of Byzantine provenance.

sites.name: San Marco Evangelista
sites.address: Palazzo Venezia, Piazza di S. Marco, 48, 00186 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: Venice's church in Rome, keeping a golden 9th-century apse mosaic.
sites.description: The national church of Venice in Rome, first consecrated in the 4th century, but rebuilt in the 9th. Noted for its surviving 9th century Byzantine apse mosaic, and its portico and loggia made from spolia from the Colosseum.

sites.name: San Martino ai Monti
alternateNames: Santi Silvestro e Martino ai Monti
Saints Sylvester & Martin in the Mountains
sites.address: Vle del Monte Oppio, 28, 00184 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: Ancient titular church rebuilt on its early plan, richly Baroque within.
sites.description: A church built in the 4th century, and rebuilt subsequently in the 6th, 8th, and 9th, following the plan and using many materials of the ancient church. The decoration and interior is mostly from the 17th century.

sites.name: San Saba
sites.address: Piazza Gian Lorenzo Bernini, 20, 00153 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: Hilltop monastic church founded by monks fleeing the conquest of Palestine.
sites.description: A church with roots in the 7th century, founded by monks of St. Sabas who were forced to flee the Islamic invasion of Palestine. Extensively renovated in the 13th century with frescoes and cosmatesque flooring. Note the ancient spolia columns.

sites.name: San Silvestro in Capite
alternateNames: Basilica of Saint Sylvester the First
sites.address: Piazza di S.Silvestro, 17A, 00187 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: Britain's national church in Rome, built over a temple to Sol Invictus.
sites.description: The national church of Great Britain in Rome, founded in the 8th century atop the ruins of a pagan temple to Sol Invictus, and extensively renovated in the 16th and 17th centuries

sites.name: Basilica of Saint Agatha of the Goths
sites.summary: Rare Arian Gothic church that still keeps a Byzantine-rite feast.
sites.description: A church built for the Arian Goths in the 5th century, rededicated in the 6th, restored in the 9th, and partiall rebuilt in the 17th. Little remains of the original Byzantine-era church, although the feast of the Greek martyrs on December 2nd is celebrated with a mass of the Byzantine Catholic rite.

sites.name: San Gregorio Magno al Celio
sites.address: Piazza di San Gregorio al Celio 1, 00184 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: Monastery founded by Gregory the Great, once papal envoy to Byzantium.
sites.description: Begun as a simple oratorio in the late 6th century by Pope St. Gregory the Great himself, who had spent years in Constantinople as papal legate to the Byzantine Court and dedicated to St. Andrew the Apostle

sites.name: Sant'Anastasia al Palatino
alternateNames: Basilica of St. Anastasia on the Palatine
sites.address: Piazza di Sant'Anastasia, 1, 00186 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: Ancient church below the Palatine, much restored over the centuries.
sites.description: A church begun in the 4th century and restored several times. While beautiful inside, little of the earlier Byzantine era remains.

sites.name: Santa Cecilia in Trastevere
sites.address: Piazza di Santa Cecilia, 22, 00153 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: Trastevere basilica over the saint's house, with a radiant 9th-century mosaic.
sites.description: The first church here was built in the 3rd century, but the current church dates to 822, when the relics of St. Cecilia were moved there. The church contains a wonderful 9th century apse mosaic.

sites.name: Santa Croce in Gerusalemme
alternateNames: Basilica of the Holy Cross in Jerusalem
sites.address: Piazza di S. Croce in Gerusalemme, 10, 00185 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: Basilica built for the Passion relics St Helena brought from Jerusalem.
sites.description: A basilica consecrated in the 4th century to house the relics of the Passion of Jesus Christ, brought to Rome by St. Helena, mother of Emperor Constantine. The floor was covered with soil from Jersualem, making the church symbolically extraterritorial, and thus "in" Jerusalem.

sites.name: Santa Lucia in Selci
sites.address: Via in Selci, 82, 00184 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: Ancient church built above the ruins of the Portico of Livia, restored by Maderno and Borromini
sites.description: A church begun either in the 6th or 7th century, during the Byzantine era dedicated to St. Lucy, a martyr of the early church. Little is left of the original interior.

sites.name: Santa Maria in Ara Coeli
alternateNames: Basilica of Saint Mary of the Altar in Heaven
sites.address: Scala dell'Arce Capitolina, 12, 00186 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: A church with Byzantine roots and containing relics from St. Helena and a famous Byzantine icon.
sites.description: This basilica is located on the peak of the Capitoline Hill, on the former site of the temple to Juno, built on the site of a previous Byzantine abbey to house relics brought from Jersualem by St. Helena, mother of Constantine. Among much notable art and history, the church also contains the Madonna Aracoeli, a 10th century Byzantine icon

sites.name: Santa Maria della Concezione in Campo Marzio
sites.address: Piazza in Campo Marzio, 45, 00186 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: A church with roots in the Byzantine iconoclastic controversy, housing relics of St. Gregory of Nazianus
sites.description: A church whose origins reach to iconoclastic controversy, when  Basilian nuns fled Constantinope in the 8th century, bringing with them relics of St. Gregory of Nazianus - now mostly returned to Constantinople - and now serves as the seat of Syrian Catholic Patriarchate of Antioch. Contains a 12th century icon of Madonna Advocata (Hagiosoritissa)

sites.name: Santa Maria in Cosmedin
sites.address: Piazza della Bocca della Verità, 18, 00186 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: A church founded for Rome's Byzantine Greek community, now the patriarchal procurate in Rome for the Melkite Greek Catholic Church.
sites.description: A church founded by monks from the Kosmidion monastery in Constantinople who fled to Rome when their monastery was destroyed by the Persian-Avar siege of 626 and built in a Greek quarter of medieval Rome. Bypass the line of tourists waiting to take pictures with a manhole cover and go right into the church to see the 8th century mosaic and the Theotokos icon.

sites.name: Santa Maria in Domnica
alternateNames: Basilica di Santa Maria in Domnica alla Navicella
sites.address: Via della Navicella, 10, 00184 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: A church rebuilt in the 9th century to include stunning apse mosaics
sites.description: Originally built in antiquity and rebuilt in the 9th century to include stunning mosaics in the triumphal arch and the apse

sites.name: Santa Maria in Tempulo
sites.address: Via di Valle delle Camene, 00184 Caracalla, Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: A church legendarily founded by exiles from Constantinople who carried an icon of the Virgin painted by St. Luke with them, now deconsecrated
sites.description: A deconsecrated former convent church which housed an icon of the Virgin Hagiosoritissa said to be painted by St. Luke and brought from Constantinople. The icon was carried across Rome by St. Dominic in 1221 when the convent was closed, and now resides in Santa Maria del Rosario on Monte Mario

sites.name: Maria Advocata - Santa Maria del Rosario on Monte Mario
sites.address: Via Alberto Cadlolo, 51, 00136 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: One of the oldest icons in Rome, said to be painted by St. Luke himself, now housed in the Church of the Madonna del Rosario
sites.description: Housed here is an icon of Mary, commonly dated to the 6th century, but possibly earlier, said to be painted by St. Luke by medieval tradition. Done with a Syriac/Egyptian technique, this is one of the oldest Marian icons in Rome.

sites.name: Santa Maria in Trastevere
alternateNames: Basilica di Santa Maria in Trastevere
sites.address: Piazza di Santa Maria in Trastevere, 00153 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: Stunning mosaics and an 8th century Marian icon adorn this Trastevere gem
sites.description: A visually stunning basilica church with excellent 12th century mosaics and a (probably) 8th century icon of Madonna della Clemenza, one of the oldest medieval Marian icons

sites.name: Santa Maria Maggiore
alternateNames: Papal Basilica of Saint Mary the Great
sites.address: P.za di Santa Maria Maggiore, 00100 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: An artistic powerhouse, this papal basilica is not to be missed, with its ancient icon of Mary, its 5th century mosaics, and its numerous notable tombs
sites.description: An unmissable Byzantine-era landmark, with extensive 5th century mosaics, among the earliest depictions of the Virgin Mary in Christian late antiquity, and mosaics in the apse, arch, and nave, and the icon Salus Populi Romani, among the oldest Marian icons in Rome. This papal basilica is the burial place of several popes, St. Jerome, and Gian Lorenzo Bernini

sites.name: Santa Prassede
sites.address: Via di Santa Prassede, 9/a, 00184 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: A basilica with ancient frescoes and mosaics, decorated by Pope St. Paschal I, who himself is depicted in mosaics in three major Roman churches
sites.description: This 8th-9th century church is notable for its ancient frescoes and its mosaics in the apse, the apsidal arch, and the triumphal arch, as well as mosaics in the attached chapel of St. Zeno, built by Pope St. Paschal for his mother, Theodora.

sites.name: Santa Prisca
sites.address: Via di Santa Prisca, 11, 00153 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: A church founded in the Byzantine age, what is extant now dates to much later. However, it sits on a fascinating Mithraeum, offering a window into an even more ancient cult.
sites.description: Although the church on the site now dates to much later, there was a 4th century church here, built over a temple of Mithras. The current church and decoration are much more modern.

sites.name: Santa Pudenziana
sites.summary: A basilica housing a very early, 4th century mosaic that prefigures the Byzantine technique
sites.description: This church was the original residence of the pope, until Constantine gave the Lateran Palace, and St. Peter is said to have lived here for a time. Inside, a 4th century mosaic offers insight into the transition of mosaic work from the ancient Roman style toward the Byzantine style, perhaps belonging to neither category.

sites.name: Santo Stefano Rotondo
alternateNames: Basilica of St. Stephen in the Round on the Caelian Hill
sites.address: Via Santo Stefano Rotondo, 7, 00184 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: An ancient, circular-plan church founded under Constantine and containing some 7th century mosaics in a chapel, but most noted for its grisly frescoes of martyrdom.
sites.description: A Byzantine-era, circular-plan church, first built in the 4th century under Constantine, and embellished in the 6th and 7th centuries with mosaics. However, much of the current décor consists of Renaissance frescoes of martyrdom, not for the faint of heart.

sites.name: Basilica of Saints Cosmas and Damian
sites.address: Via dei Fori Imperiali, 1, 00186 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: A former Forum temple converted to a church in the 6th century, SS Cosmas and Damian contains important early Romano-Byzantine mosaics.
sites.description: Originally a Roman temple inside the Forum (whose church entrance faces the Forum on the Via dei Fori Imperiali), this was converted to a church in 527, and contains important early mosaics, melding the Roman and Byzantine styles.

sites.name: Basilica Santi Giovanni e Paolo
alternateNames: Basilica of Saints John and Paul on the Caelian Hill
sites.address: Piazza dei Santi Giovanni e Paolo, 13, 00184 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: A church rooted in the Byzantine age with more modern art and architecture.
sites.description: Originally built in 398, this church has its roots in the Byzantine age. However, a series of lootings and restorations mean the current church bears little resemblance to earlier times.

sites.name: Chiesa dei Santi Luca e Martina Martiri
sites.address: Via della Curia, 2, 00184 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: A church rooted in the Byzantine age, updated in the Baroque style.
sites.description: A church with roots in the 7th century, and found within the Forum of Rome, it was extensively rebuilt beginning in the 17th century, and bears little resemblance to its early past.

sites.name: Basilica of Saints Nereus and Achilleus
sites.address: Viale delle Terme di Caracalla, 28, 00153 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: An unassuming titular basilica by the Baths of Caracalla, this is worth seeing for its 9th century mosaics, but it is open less than 100 hours per year.
sites.description: A 4th century basilica church outside the Baths of Caracalla, restored in the 15th and 17th centuries, the apse contains 9th century mosaics of the Annunciation, the Transfiguration, and Mary and Child.

sites.name: Madonna of Santa Maria in Via Lata
alternateNames: Madonna Advocata of Santa Maria in Via Lata
sites.address: V. del Corso, 306, 00186 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: A 12th century icon of the Virgin Hagiosoritissa, inscribed Stella Maris
sites.description: On the high altar of the Church of Santa Maria in Via Lata, in an ornate baroque frame, sits the 12th century icon of Maria Advocata, or the Virgin Hagiosoritissa, gesturing to the viewer's left. It is also inscribed as Stella Maris, and many miracles have been attributed to it.

sites.name: Church of Saints Sergius and Bacchus
alternateNames: Cattedrale della Madonna del Pascolo e dei Santi Sergio e Bacco degli Ucraini
sites.address: Piazza della Madonna dei Monti, 3, 00184 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: A Byzantine Rite Catholic Church with a copy of the icon of Our Lady of Zyrowice
sites.description: A Byzantine Rite Catholic church in Monti, it is unclear exactly when this church was built. It now contains an icon of Our Lady of Zyrowice, or Our Lady of the Pasture, said to have been discovered under the plaster of the sacristy wall.

sites.name: St. Agnes Outside the Walls
alternateNames: Basilica di Sant'Agnese Fuori le Mura
sites.summary: A basilica church atop the catacombs, this contains important 4th century mosaics that have survived very well
sites.description: Attached to the mausoleum of Constantina, daughter of Constantine I, this basilica contains very notable 4th century mosaics with early depictions of Jesus and of St. Agnes dressed as a Byzantine empress.

sites.name: St. George in Velabro
sites.address: San Giorgio in Velabro, Via del Velabro, 19, 00186 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: An early church in the Greek quarter of Rome and incorporating a 3rd century Roman arch
sites.description: Perhaps as early as the 4th century, a church stood here in the Greek quarter of Rome, or Schola Graeca, housing the relics of St. George, brought here from Cappadocia. The current plan is oddly trapezoidal, due to extensive renovations and rebuildings.

sites.name: St. Paul Outside the Walls
alternateNames: Papal Basilica of Saint Paul Outside the Walls
sites.address: Piazzale San Paolo, 1, 00146 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: A major papal basilica founded by Constantine the Great on the burial site of St. Paul, outside the Aurelian Walls of Rome. Noted for its extensive and gorgeous restored mosaics.
sites.description: Extremely worth the short train ride from central Rome, this church, once situated on the outskirts outside of the Aurelian Walls, contains extensive and stunning mosaics, along with the burial site of St. Paul. First built by Constantine, this church was devastated by fire and largely rebuilt in the 19th century, but remains among the most notable sites in the world.

sites.name: Orthodox Church of Saint Theodore at the Palatine Hill
sites.address: Via di S. Teodoro, 7, 00187 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: The only Greek Orthodox church in Rome, San Toto, as it is affectionately know, contains a beautiful 6th century apse mosaic
sites.description: Now given to the use of the Greek Orthodox Church, this sanctuary contains a 6th century apse mosaic of Jesus in Roman garments of high rank, along with later, 13th century additions

sites.name: St. Peter's Basilica
alternateNames: Papal Basilica of Saint Peter in the Vatican
sites.address: Piazza San Pietro, 00120 Città del Vaticano, Vatican City
sites.summary: The best-known church of Roman Catholicism, St. Peter's was founded by Constantine in the 4th century. The present building is Renaissance through and through, but there is plenty for the explorer to find.
sites.description: While Old St. Peter's was begun by the emperor Constantine in the 4th century and long held the relics of the Three Holy Hierarchs, the current building dates to the 16th and 17th centuries. However, sharp eyes will notice the spiral Solomonic Columns, the monumental bronze doors depicting the Council of Florence-Ferrara and Emperor John VIII Palaiologos, and John VII's mosaics, relocated to the Vatican Grottoes. And be sure you don't miss the Equestrian Statue of Constantine, by Bernini

sites.name: Vatican Museums
sites.summary: Incredible and far-ranging museum that contains a fair few striking Byzantine finds for the sharp-eyed visitor
sites.description: The Byzantine connoisseur will find much to admire here, from the room of Greek and Russian icons, the Museo Sacro full of Byzantine ivories, reliquaries, and enamels, along with the showstopper: the porphyry sarcophagi of the family of Constantine and Helena.

sites.name: Mausoleum of Helena
alternateNames: Mausoleum of Saint Elena Tor Pignattara
sites.summary: The ruin of the mausoleum of St. Helena, built by Constantine near the Roman catacombs
sites.description: A mausoleum built by Emperor Cosntantine, probably originally for himself, but given to his mother Helena on her death in 330. An imposing ruin, but not much to see otherwise, especially since the monumental porphyry sarcophagus of St. Helena now resides in the Vatican Museums.

sites.name: Santa Balbina
sites.address: Piazza di Santa Balbina, 8, 00153 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: A minor basilica on the Aventine with a Constantinian legend and a 4th century provenance
sites.description: A pleasant and quiet minor Basilica on the Aventine from the 4th century, this church is said to be where Constantine bade farewell to the pope before he went east to found his city.

sites.name: Papal Basilica of Saint Lawrence outside the Walls
sites.address: Piazzale del Verano, 3, 00185 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: A papal minor basilica with 6th century mosaics on the triumphal arch
sites.description: Built on the site of an oratory built by Constantine I on the burial site of St. Lawrence, the 6th century church contains surviving contemporary Byzantine mosaics on the triumphal arch.

sites.name: Milvian Bridge
sites.summary: The site of the famous battle that established Constantine as sole emperor, mediated by his vision of a divine sign
sites.description: A 2nd century pedestrian bridge that survives to this day, this site is most famous for being the site of the Battle of the Milvian Bridge, establishing Constantine as sole emperor after his victory, mediated by his vision of the sign under which he would conquer.

sites.name: Santa Maria Antiqua
sites.address: 00186 Rome, Metropolitan City of Rome Capital, Italy
sites.summary: A 6th century church inside the Roman Forum, this church contains extensive and important pre-Iconoclasm wall paintings.
sites.description: Built in the 6th century, this church is widely noted for its extensive and indeed important collection of 6th-8th century wall paintings, which together make up one of the largest collections of pre-Iconoclasm Roman-Byzantine art in the world.

sites.name: San Marco Evangelista al Campidoglio
sites.address: Palazzo Venezia, Piazza di S. Marco, 48, 00186 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: A 9th century rebuild of this church provided it with stunning apse mosaics.
sites.description: First built in 334, this church was rebuilt in the 9th century, at which point it picked up a set of gorgeous mosaics in the apse.

sites.name: Santa Sabina all'Aventino
sites.address: Piazza Pietro D'Illiria, 1, 00153 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: An architecturally traditional basilica with 5th century wooden doors
sites.description: This 5th century basilica is the oldest church to retain its staid, stately ecclesiastical basilica style, mostly interesting to historians of the era for its indication of the origins of the architecture. However, one should not miss the 5th century cypress doors.

sites.name: Madonna di Sant'Alessio
sites.address: P.za di Sant'Alessio, 23, 00153 Roma RM, Italy
sites.summary: A 12th century icon of the Virgin Hagiosoritissa, brought from Edessa
sites.description: Housed in the Basilica of the Saints Bonifacio and Alexis on the Aventine, this 12th century icon is of Byzantine origin, said to have been brought to Rome from Edessa, perhaps by St. Alexis himself. A fine example of the Panagia Hagiosoritissa.

sites.name: Church of Panagia Kapnikarea
sites.summary: A center-city 11th century Byzantine church, and one of the oldest continuously in use
sites.description: A Byzantine church from the 11th century right in the middle of bustling Athens, this is one of the oldest churches continuously in use in the city. Probably once the katholikon of a monastery, the church itself is domed cross-in-square.

sites.name: Santa Maria de Taüll
alternateNames: Church of St. Mary of Tahull
sites.address: Plaça Sta Maria, 1, 25528 Taüll, Lleida, Spain
sites.summary: Two Catalan churches with directly Byzantine art, including a Pantokrator and enthroned Theotokos, transmitted through trading links to Italy
sites.description: To be clear, the Catalan Pyrenees were never Byzantine, nor was this site occupied by Greek refugees. However, the visual language of the church is clearly derived from Byzantium, albeit at the far edge of its diffusion, a thousand miles from Constantinople

sites.name: Sant Climent de Taüll
alternateNames: Church of St. Clement of Tahull
sites.address: Avinguda de les Freixes, 25528 Taüll, Lleida, Spain
sites.summary: Two Catalan churches with directly Byzantine art, including a Pantokrator and enthroned Theotokos, transmitted through trading links to Italy
sites.description: One of two sister churches in Vall de Boí, Catalonia, Sant Climent speaks the visual language of Byzantium, derived from trading links with Italy. Note the Pantokrator in the apse, emblematic of the Catalan Romanesque, and directly Byzantine in derivation.

sites.name: Museum of Byzantine and Medieval Abruzzo
sites.address: Castello Ducale, Piazza Castello, 4, 66014 Crecchio CH, Italy
sites.summary: A museum centered on finds from 6th-7th century Roman-Byzantine villa
sites.description: A museum centered on finds from 6th-7th century Roman-Byzantine villa, tied to the Ravenna Exarchate and engaged in trade with the wider empire.

sites.name: Poganovo Monastery
alternateNames: Monastery of Saint John the Theologian Poganovo
sites.summary: A monastery closely connected to the Palaiologan emperors and with beautiful 15th century late-Byzantine frescoes
sites.description: A Serbian Orthodox monastery founded by Konstantin Dragaš, father of Helena Dragaš, who became the mother of the last two Byzantine emperors, brother John VIII and Constantine XI. Its late 15th century frescoes are gems of Balkan late-Byzantine art.

sites.name: Bachkovo Monastery
alternateNames: Bachkovo Monastery of the Dormition of the Theotokos
Monastery of the Mother of God Petritzonitissa
sites.summary: One of Bulgaria's greatest monasteries, with a tricultural heritage, 12th century Komnenian frescoes, and a notable icon
sites.description: Founded in the late 11th century by the megas domestikos of the western armies of Alexios I Komnenos, this site is tricultural: Byzantine, Georgian, and Bulgarian. Note the well-preserved Komnenian frescoes of the 12th century and the icon of the Virgin of Eleusa, brought from Georgia and hidden in the mountains during the Ottoman occupation.

sites.name: St. Clement of Ohrid
alternateNames: Church of Sts. Clement and Panteleimon at Plaošnik
sites.address: 4Q7R+F5X, MK, Kuzman Kapidan, Ohrid 6000, North Macedonia
sites.summary: A modern church on the original site of St. Clement's life and work
sites.description: This is the historically authentic site of St. Clement's life, school, and tomb, originally built in 890; however, the Ottomans demolished it to the foundations and built a mosque on top. Thankfully, a new church was built on the site in 2002 in the Byzantine style, and St. Clement was laid to rest there once again.

sites.name: Church of St. Erasmus
sites.summary: A cave church near Ohrid with 13th century frescoes
sites.description: Tucked into a rock face on Gabovski Hill along the Ohrid–Struga road, about 5 km from Ohrid, this church contains 13th century frescoes and sits near 6th-12th century Christian gravesites.

sites.name: Saint Naum Monastery
sites.summary: A 10th century monastery with a 16th century Byzantine church
sites.description: At the southern tip of Lake Ohrid, about 29 km south of town right by the Albanian border, this monastery was founded in 905 by St. Naum himself. The original 9th century trefoil church was destroyed, but the site now holds a multi-domed Byzantine church built in the 16th century.

sites.name: Treskavec Monastery
sites.address: Holy Mother of God, Северна, North Macedonia
sites.summary: A layered and difficult to access religious complex whose core is a Palaiologan church with beautiful frescoes.
sites.description: The single-nave domed church has a 12th-century core, but its defining phase came at the end of the 13th and start of the 14th century — above all the outer porch — under the patronage of the Byzantine general Michael Doukas Glabas Tarchaneiotes, protostrator under Andronikos II and Michael IX Palaiologos, whose donor portrait survives above the main entrance. Lovely frescoes round out the church.

sites.name: Asteriou Monastery of the Taxiarchs
sites.summary: A working monastery with 16th century structures and wall paintings and an unclear founding date
sites.description: A fuzzy foundation legend puts this monastery either in the 5th century or the 10th century, the latter suggesting that Hosios Loukas lived here as a young monk. However, the architectural structures and wall paintings date to the 16th century. Pilgrims are welcome in the mornings, but it is a working monastery and often closed.

sites.name: Hymettus
sites.summary: A mountain near Athens with hikes and views, along with various working monasteries and other Byzantine remnants
sites.description: A mountain east of Athens in Attica offering superb hiking and views over the city, but also containing Byzantine monasteries and various smaller Byzantine foundations including St. John the Hunter (Agios Ioannis Kyrigos) from the 12th century, St. John the Theologian near Papagou with lovely wall paintings, and Agios Ioannis Prodomos (Kareas) perhaps from the 12th century.

sites.name: Kaisariani Monastery
sites.summary: This 12th century monastery, renowned as a scholarly center at its peak, retains gorgeous late- and post-Byzantine frescoes
sites.description: A cross-in-square katholikon dedicated to the Presentation of the Virgin, its interior covered in exquisite post-Byzantine frescoes by Athonite masters. At its late-12th/early-13th-century peak it was the richest and most renowned monastery on the mountain, famed for a library that drew scholars; in 1458 Mehmed II reportedly received the keys of Athens here.

sites.name: Old Port of Classe
sites.address: Via Marabina, 7 Zona Ponte Nuovo-Classe, 48124 Ravenna RA, Italy
sites.summary: An extremely important port of the Byzantine era, conquered by Belisarius, now an active archaeological site
sites.description: The old port of Ravenna, now inland due to silting of the Po River and sinking several inches every year, it is an active archaeological site and museum. Long an extremely important hub for the Byzantine Empire and the Exarchate of Ravenna, Belisarius took this port in 540 in the Gothic Wars and the empire held it for more than 200 years after.

sites.name: Basilica di San Severo in Classe
alternateNames: Basilica of St. Severus in Classe
sites.address: Via Romea Sud, 48124 Ravenna RA, Italy
sites.summary: An archaeological site near its still-standing sister basilica. As of this writing it is not open to the public, but it is slated to become a visitable part of the archaeological park.
sites.description: One of three basilicas within a stone's throw, just up the road from Sant'Apollinare in Classe, this one was totally destroyed, but is now an active archaeological site. Dedicated to St. Severus of Ravenna, whose image you will see in the Justinianic mosaics at Sant'Apollinare in Classe.

sites.name: Vezneciler Cistern
sites.address: Süleymaniye, Darülfünun Cd. No:2, 34116 Fatih/İstanbul, Türkiye
sites.summary: An unnamed minor cistern uncovered during road construction in central Istanbul
sites.description: With no known Greek name and very little left to see amid the hustle and bustle of central Istanbul, Vezneciler Cistern can be easy to miss. Sharp-eyed visitors will notice the Byzantine arches that once held water for the neighborhood.

sites.name: Cistern of Modestus
sites.address: Kalenderhane Mah Atatürk Bulvarı, Şehzadebaşı Cd., 34134 Fatih/İstanbul, Türkiye
sites.summary: A non-visitable cistern underlying a public park in modern Istanbul
sites.description: Nothing left to see of the cistern itself, which underlies the park, but the whole area sits under the shadow of the Aqueduct of Valens, a monumental site.

sites.name: Cistern of Aetius
sites.address: Karagümrük, Keçeci Meydanı Sk. No:13, 34091 Fatih/İstanbul, Türkiye
sites.summary: A modern soccer stadium that sits atop a Byzantine cistern
sites.description: You may be wondering why this soccer field sits so much lower than the street level around it. Wonder no more - it is the Cistern of Aetius. Or rather, it sits upon the footprint of the cistern, though nothing much of the original remains to be seen.

sites.name: Cistern of Aspar
sites.address: Balat, Sultan Selim Cd., 34087 Fatih/İstanbul, Türkiye
sites.summary: A Byzantine cistern that now holds a park, with its masonry borders still visible
sites.description: The most interesting thing about this park, which sits noticeably below the surrounding street level, is what you'll see along its borders. The whole park, which was the Cistern of Aspar, and its masonry remains visible. "Çukurbostan" means something like "sunken garden."

sites.name: Cistern of Mocius
sites.address: Seyyid Ömer, Köprülüzade Sk., 34200 Fatih/İstanbul, Türkiye
sites.summary: A Byzantine cistern that now holds a park, with its masonry borders still visible
sites.description: This park sits noticeably below street level, and indeed its name includes the Turkish word "Çukurbostan," meaning sunken garden. That is because it sits within the former Cistern of Mocius, named for the now-gone Church of St. Mocius nearby. It was built somewhere within the late 5th and early 6th century on Constantinople's seventh hill.

sites.name: Pantokrator Cistern
sites.address: Cibali, Atatürk Blv. No:21, 34083 Fatih/İstanbul, Türkiye
sites.summary: Street-level visible cistern masonry, once a part of the great Monastery of Christ Pantokrator complex
sites.description: Fully visible at street level along Atatürk Boulevard, the remains of this cistern belonged to the complex of the great Monastery of Christ Pantokrator (now called Molla Zeyrek Mosque), one of the most important Byzantine sites in the city. You can visit this one, and there is a teahouse inside.

sites.name: Basilica Cistern
sites.summary: An underground Justinianic cistern in the heart of the old city's historic center
sites.description: This Justinianic cistern from the 6th century sat below, and is named for, the Stoa Basilica. It is the most famous and well-trafficked of the city's cisterns, and it is indeed well worth a visit.

sites.name: Acımusluk Street Cistern
sites.address: Hobyar, Cemal Nadir Sk. No:33 D:27, 34112 Fatih/İstanbul, Türkiye
sites.summary: A small Byzantine cistern repurposed as an Ottoman jail then left to deteriorate
sites.description: A small Byzantine cistern, repurposed by the Ottomans as a jail, and allowed to become a neighborhood trash dump. Masonry and columns are still somewhat visible, but there are better cisterns to visit.

sites.name: Rotunda Cistern of Myrelaion
sites.address: Mesih Paşa, Aksaray Cd. No:17 34130, 34130 Fatih/İstanbul, Türkiye
sites.summary: A 10th century cistern occupied by clothing sellers and open to the public
sites.description: Built in the 5th century as a rotunda, repurposed to a cistern by Romanos I Lekapenos in the 10th century on which he built his palace. Named for the Myrelaion Church nearby and now occupied by clothing sellers.

sites.name: Gülhane Park Cistern
sites.summary: A former Byzantine cistern in a pleasant park, now a cultural space
sites.description: The Gülhane Park Cistern, conveniently in Gülhane Park, is generally dated to the 5th-7th centuries and is now open to the public as a cultural and art space.

sites.name: Byzantine Cistern in Sultantepe, Üsküdar
sites.summary: Visible remains of a cistern on the Asian side of Istanbul
sites.description: A visible ruined cistern on the Asian side of the Bosphorus, in the zone of ancient Chrysopolis, the Byzantine settlement facing Constantinople across the water. Byzantine remains can be rare here, but there is not much to visit. No name is historically attested.

sites.name: Basilica di San Pietro in Ciel d'Oro
sites.address: Piazza S. Pietro in Ciel d'Oro, 27100 Pavia PV, Italy
sites.summary: An 8th century Augustiniain church noted for its gold leaf mosaic apse
sites.description: An 8th century basilica and monastery church used by Augustinian friars and noted for being the resting place of St. Augustine of Hippo. The name (golden sky) refers to the golden mosaics of the apse. The modern church owes most of its structure to a 12th century reconstruction.

sites.name: Church of Saint Michael in Africisco
alternateNames: Chiesa di San Michele in Africisco
sites.address: Via IV Novembre, 37, 48121 Ravenna RA, Italy
sites.summary: The remains of one of Ravenna's great mosaiced churches, now just a few fragments visible in a shop
sites.description: Bearing the dubious distinction of being Ravenna's only major Byzantine church whose art was dispersed, the site today houses a commercial shop, but parts of the apse and a 15th century chapel are still visible, along with a bell tower. Africisco (ad Frigiselo) likely referred to the neighborhood. The great mosaics are now in the Bode Museum, Berlin

sites.name: Bode-Museum
sites.summary: A museum with Byzantine sculpture and mosaic, largely from Ravenna
sites.description: A museum which now houses, among other exhibits, Byzantine sculpture from Constantinople and Ravenna, as well as the mosaics from St. Michael in Africisco, Ravenna, which were sold to King Frederick William IV of Prussia in the 19th century

sites.name: Chapel of St. Mary Formosa
sites.summary: A 6th century church with mosaics and wall paintings in the style of Ravenna
sites.description: A 6th century Greek cross church, built by Maximianus, later Archbishop of Ravenna. The floors and walls are decorated with 6th century mosaics, and it has drawn comparison to the Ravenna mausoleum of Galla Placidia.

sites.name: Chiesa della Panaghia
sites.address: Via S. Giovanni di Dio, 5, 87064 Corigliano-Rossano CS, Italy
sites.summary: A small, 11th century Byzantine church with notable brickwork and fragmentary frescoes
sites.description: A small church built during the Byzantine period in Calabria, including decorative brickwork and fragmentary frescoes showing St. John Chrysostom and St. Basil of Caesarea from the 13th-14th century. No official opening hours, but if you ask at the museum or a nearby coffee shop, someone will find a key for you.

sites.name: Butrint Baptistery
sites.summary: A 6th century baptistery repurposed from a Roman bath, with noted mosaic flooring and inscriptions
sites.description: A 6th century baptistery that cleverly reused a Roman hypocaust for the rite of baptism. Decorated by notable mosaic floors, it was excavated in the 20th century. Visitors may not always see the floors, however, as they are covered with sand to protect them from rising and falling water levels in the surrounding lagoon.

sites.name: Fortress of Timgad
alternateNames: Byzantine Fort on the Aqua Septimiana Felix
sites.summary: A 6th century fortress erected during the Justinianic reconquest of North Africa
sites.description: Constructed by the Byzantines during Justinians reconquest of North Africa in the mid-6th century, it reused much material from earlier Roman structures nearby and remains one of the better-preserved Byzantine military sites in Africa.

sites.name: Trieste Cathedral
sites.address: P.za della Cattedrale, 2, 34121 Trieste TS, Italy
sites.summary: A layered and ancient structure with notable 12th-13th century apse mosaics
sites.description: This cathedral and minor basilica has its foundations in a Roman propylaea, then a 6th century church (whose mosaic floors are still partially visible), and finally a 14th century building. Most notable are the apsidal mosaics by Veneto-Byzantine master craftsmen, laid in the 12th-13th centuries.

sites.name: Vazelon Monastery
sites.address: Coşandere, Maçka Yolu No:36, 61750 Maçka/Trabzon, Türkiye
sites.summary: An abandoned monastery with a long and storied history, now deteriorating
sites.description: A large and historically important multistory monastery complex with a 1700 year history, now abandoned due to the genocide of the Pontic Greeks, with deteriorating and vandalized Christian artwork

sites.name: Trabzon Castle
sites.address: Ortahisar, Burç Sk. No:10, 61030 Trabzon Merkez/Trabzon, Türkiye
sites.summary: A series of city fortifications that housed the palace of the Empire of Trebizond
sites.description: Commonly called a castle, this is a series of fortifications and city walls, including a citadel that contained the imperial palace of the Grand Komnenoi of the Empire of Trebizond. Substantial sections survive.

sites.name: Hagia Sophia Trabzon
sites.address: Fatih, Ayasofya Cd. No:60, 61040 Ortahisar/Trabzon, Türkiye
sites.summary: An exemplar of late Byzantine architecture and 13th-14th century fresco, reconverted from a museum to a mosque
sites.description: An important example of late Byzantine architecture, this church was completed in the 13th century with some surviving frescoes of the Palaiologan Renaissance. Converted to a mosque after the Ottoman conquest, it was then made a museum and then sadly reconverted to a mosque, covering the beautiful art and floors.

sites.name: Panagia Chrysokephalos
sites.address: Ortahisar, Fatih Cami Sk. No:6, 61030 Trabzon Merkez/Trabzon, Türkiye
sites.summary: The most important church of the Empire of Trebizond, with much of its beauty destroyed when made into a mosque
sites.description: While much older than the Empire of Trebizond, this church - the metropolitan, coronation, and funerary church of the Grand Komnenoi and the cathedral of Trebizond - reached its height in the 12th century. Now it is a mosque, with its frescoes poorly painted over and wood floors dropped on its opus sectile floor.

sites.name: Hagios Eugenios Church
sites.address: Yenicuma, Cami Sk. No:48, 61030, 61030 Trabzon Merkez/Trabzon, Türkiye
sites.summary: A church with a largely 13th century structure, but with its art destroyed by the Ottomans
sites.description: The structure of this church was rebuilt after Ottoman destruction in the 13th century. Subsequent destruction after the conquest of the Ottomans caused the destruction of its art.

sites.name: St. Anne Church
sites.address: Çarşı, Mısırlıoğlı Ar. No:7, 61200 Trabzon Merkez/Trabzon, Türkiye
sites.summary: An early Byzantine church restored very recently to reveal its frescoes
sites.description: A small, early Byzantine church of unknown date, restored in the 9th century. It was restored again in 2021-22 to remove the whitewash and make the frescoes visible again.

sites.name: Sümela Monastery
sites.address: Altindere Valley National Park, Altındere, 61750 Maçka/Trabzon, Türkiye
sites.summary: A dramatic cliffside monastery, now a museum and visitable by the public
sites.description: Perched precariously on a cliff outside Trebizond, this monastery is now a museum. Preserved after the Ottoman conquest, it retains its frescoes, its rock church, chapels, monks' quarters, and a library. Made a museum after the Treaty of Lausanne.

sites.name: Metropolitan Cathedral of Panagia Spilaiotissa
sites.summary: A later church housing the remains of St. Theodora Augusta, the empress who helped end iconoclasm
sites.description: A Venetian church of the 16th century, he Byzantine link is its great relic: the holy body of St. Theodora Augusta, the Byzantine empress who championed the restoration of icons after the Iconoclast period, transferred to Corfu in the mid-1450s as Constantinople fell.

sites.name: Galatista Byzantine Tower
sites.summary: A late Byzantine square tower in Chalkidiki
sites.description: In the middle of Galatista village in Chalkidiki stands a classic late-Byzantine square tower, built in the 11th century and added to in the 14th.

sites.name: Church of St. George of Samatya
sites.address: Koca Mustafapaşa, Marmara Cd. No:47, 34098 Fatih/İstanbul, Türkiye
sites.summary: A modern church built atop two previous Byzantine churches
sites.description: A modern, 19th century Armenian church built atop the 11th century Byzantine church to St. Mary Peribleptos, itself built atop a 5th century church to Hagios Stephanos. Only the Byzantine foundations remain; however the church shows up on Cristoforo Buondelmonti's famous map

sites.name: Chapel of St. Catherine
sites.summary: A frescoed funerary chapel inside the castle
sites.description: A Late Byzantine funerary chapel inside the castle, standing beside the church of Agios Athanasios and close to the site of the Byzantine palace on the Kale hill, with high-quality frescoes

sites.name: Castle of Didymoteicho
sites.summary: An important and layered Byzantine castle
sites.description: Rebuilt and strengthened throughout the Byzantine age, it's one of the most important Byzantine-era castles in Thrace and the Balkans.

sites.name: Byzantine Museum of Didymoteicho
sites.summary: A museum of Byzantine history and archaeology with a Thracian focus
sites.description: A museum that centers on the Thrace–Didymoteicho relationship, presenting the town's role in the history of the Byzantine Empire as a major administrative and military base and imperial seat.
sites.hours: 8:30–15:30 Wed, Thu, Fri, Sun; 13:00–20:00 Sat; closed Mon, Tue

sites.name: Gardiki Castle
sites.summary: A medieval fortress built by the Despot of Epirus to defend Corfu
sites.description: A medieval fortress built by the Despot of Epirus before Corfu's Venetian era; one of three castles built to defend Corfu.

sites.name: Angelokastro
sites.summary: A dramatic mountaintop castle built by the Despot of Eprius in Corfu
sites.description: A Byzantine castle built on the highest peak of the island's shoreline, commanding a dramatic view of the city of Corfu and the sea. One of three castles built to defend Corfu during the Despotate of Epirus.

sites.name: Kassiopi Castle
sites.summary: A ruined fortress used by Byzantines, Epirotes, and Venetians
sites.description: The oldest of the three castles used by the Despotate of Epirus to defend Corfu, and the worst-preserved, mostly destroyed and left to deteriorate by the Venetians.

sites.name: Sousse Archaeological Museum
sites.address: RJFP+644, Rue Abou Kacem Echabi, Sousse, Tunisia
sites.summary: A museum famous for mosaics, with a section for early Christian and Byzantine finds
sites.description: Known for its enormous collection of Roman mosaics, it also has a room of early Christian funerary mosaics and catacomb finds, plus a standout Byzantine-era mosaic-covered baptismal font from El Gaalla and the 6th-century Christian Mosaic of Theodoulus.

sites.name: Santa Maria di Mesumundu
sites.summary: A 6th century church with characteristic Byzantine masonry, rare for Sardinia
sites.description: A rare survivor of Byzantine Sardinia, the church stands on the ruins of a late-imperial Roman bath complex, and the Byzantines reused part of the Roman walls and the aqueduct. Built in the 6th century with characteristic Byzantine opus listatum

sites.name: Westminster Cathedral
sites.address: Victoria St, London SW1P 1LT, United Kingdom
sites.summary: A modern Catholic cathedral in the 9th century neo-Byzantine style
sites.description: Yes, really. Westminster Cathedral is Britain's boldest homage to Byzantium: the largest and most thorough British effort in the 9th century Neo-Byzantine style, sporting domes, marble, and gold mosaics.

sites.name: Theotokos Kosmosoteira
sites.summary: A 12th century church with frescoes modeled after its founder's Komnenian relatives
sites.description: Built in 1152 by the sebastokrator Isaac Komnenos, a son of Emperor Alexios I Komnenos (seen in a mosaic in Chora Church), later coming into the fief of 4th Crusade chronicler Geoffrey of Villehardouin. The 12th-century frescoes are a fine example of the Constantinopolitan school, including military saints given the features of Isaac's Komnenian relatives.

sites.name: Maiden's Castle
sites.address: Atakent, Mersin - Antalya Yolu, 33740 Silifke/Mersin, Türkiye
sites.summary: A 12th century island fortress connected to the Korkyros Castle by a breakwater
sites.description: At the start of the 12th century the Byzantines built this supplementary castle on the small island — later called "Maiden's Castle" from the legend of a king who shut his daughter here

sites.name: Korkyros Castle
sites.summary: A 12th century castle protecting the Byzantine town of Korkyros
sites.description: The land half of the pair of Korkyros castles, along with Maiden's Castle, connected by a breakwater, this fort was restored under Justinian and Alexios Komnenos, but lies mostly in ruins today

sites.name: Philadelphia St. Jean Church
sites.address: Soğuksu, İsmet Paşa Cd. No:114, 45600 Alaşehir/Manisa, Türkiye
sites.summary: The ruins of a large, ancient church in the former Byzantine city of Philadelphia
sites.description: The ruins stand in Alaşehir, ancient Philadelphia in Manisa province, the sixth church of Revelation. The present, ruined, structure dates to about 600, some of the massive brick pillars that once held up the dome still extant, along with sections of Byzantine wall and mosaic fragments.

sites.name: Museo della Cattedrale di Anagni
sites.address: Via Papa Leone XIII, 03012 Anagni FR, Italy
sites.summary: A cathedral and museum with medieval Byzantine frescoes, a Byzantine style icon and a copy of the Codex Justinianus
sites.description: By tradition the cathedral was completed thanks to the Byzantine Emperor Michael VII Doukas, and a Byzantine-style Madonna (c. 1250) survives on a pillar of the left aisle. Above all, the crypt of San Magno beneath the choir is entirely covered in remarkably preserved medieval frescoes, deeply Byzantine in style and often called the "Sistine Chapel of the Middle Ages." Also contains an important 1518 copy of the Codex Justinianus.

sites.name: Monastery of St. Panteleimon, Gorno Nerezi
sites.summary: An intimate 12th century church with celebrated Komnenian-era frescoes
sites.description: Built and painted in 1164 by Alexios Komnenos, nephew of the emperor, the frescoes here are the most celebrated treasure of Komnenian-era Byzantine painting, above all the "Lamentation of Christ." The main dome collapsed in 1555 and the church was renewed and repainted, with fragments of the older frescoes incorporated into the new work.

sites.name: Sbeitla Archaeological Site
sites.summary: An archaeological site in Tunisia with Byzantine walls, basilicas, and fonts
sites.description: The Byzantines made Sufetula their regional capital and military stronghold, and built the 6th-century wall around the temples, while several Early Christian basilicas, such as the Basilica of Vitalis, preserve mosaic-covered baptismal fonts in situ. After Muslims conquered the area, development stopped, and the site remains a time capsule.

sites.name: Nea Moni of Chios
sites.summary: An 11th-century monastery with excellent Macedonia Renaissance mosaics
sites.description: An 11th-century monastery high on Mount Provateio, about 15 km from Chios town, and among the finest examples of Macedonian Renaissance mosaic art. It was built in the mid-11th century by Emperor Constantine IX Monomachos and Empress Zoe. Plundered and vandalized by Turks in the 19th century

sites.name: St. Mary of the Mongols
sites.address: Balat, Firketeci Sk. No:1, 34087 Fatih/İstanbul, Türkiye
sites.summary: A 13th century church founded by an emperor's daughter, only occasionally open to the public
sites.description: The present church was established in 1281 by Maria Palaiologina, an illegitimate daughter of Michael VIII who had been sent to marry a Mongol Ilkhan and returned a widow to become a nun, hence "of the Mongols." It's the only Byzantine church in Istanbul never converted into a mosque, and it holds an 11th-century mosaic.

sites.name: Boğdan Sarayı
sites.address: Derviş Ali, Cepken Sk., 34087 Fatih/İstanbul, Türkiye
sites.summary: A ruined Palaiologan chapel in the old city
sites.description: A ruined Byzantine chapel near Chora Church. Its masonry of broad alternating bands of ashlar and brick, and its multifaceted apse, are typical of Palaiologan construction.

sites.name: Pyrohoshcha Dormition Church
sites.summary: A reconstruction of a classic 12th century, Byzantine-style, Kievan Rus' church
sites.description: This stone church was erected in 1132–1136 in the Byzantine style. It is a short church of three naves and apses under a single dome, its walls frescoed, representing a classic product of Kyivan Rus', whose church architecture came directly from Constantinople. Destroyed by the Soviets and rebuilt in the 1990s.

sites.name: Saint Sophia Cathedral
sites.summary: An 11th century Ukrainian cathedral that preserves excellent mosaics and frescoes modeled after the Byzantines'
sites.description: It was founded in 1037 by Grand Prince Yaroslav the Wise to celebrate his victory over the Pechenegs, and dedicated to Holy Wisdom, consciously modeling Kyiv on Constantinople and its great cathedral. Though its exterior was remodeled, its interior preserves an 11th-century collection of mosaics and frescoes unique for its integrity

sites.name: Cistern of the Hebdomon
sites.summary: A Byzantine cistern-cum-elephant pen showing its ancient masonry
sites.description: A Byzantine open-air reservoir in Bakırköy, the ancient Hebdomon, it supplied water to the Magnaura and the Jucundianae Palaces nearby. Later used by the Ottomans to house palace elephants.

sites.name: Senato Sarayı
sites.address: Selçuk, Surdibi Çk. No:2, 16860 İzni̇k/Bursa, Türkiye
sites.summary: An underwater archaeological site of perhaps great importance, with Byzantine structures within
sites.description: This is a monumental Roman-Byzantine structure, but it is actually underwater and only spotted by chance in 2014 aerial photographs. Excavations revealed a Byzantine basilica, probably sunk in the lake by a 740 earthquake. Some bolder archaeologists have suggested that this is the site where the Nicene Creed was promulgated.

sites.name: Cistern of Philoxenos
sites.address: Binbirdirek, İmran Öktem Cd. No:2, 34122 Fatih/İstanbul, Türkiye
sites.summary: An enormous Byzantine cistern with a grid of tall columnar supports, often two columns joined together
sites.description: A covered Byzantine cistern on the historic peninsula, near the Hippodrome and Çemberlitaş, whose Turkish name means "1,001 Columns." It's the second-largest covered cistern in Constantinople after the Basilica Cistern.

sites.name: Palace of Antiochos
sites.address: Binbirdirek, Mehmet Akif Ersoy Parkı, 34122 Fatih/İstanbul, Türkiye
sites.summary: The scattered and crumbling remains of the 5th century palace of a Byzantine court eunuch
sites.description: An early-5th-century aristocratic palace just northwest of the Hippodrome in the heart of historic Constantinople. Today, only scattered and crumbling walls remain.

sites.name: Church of St. Tryphon
sites.address: Selçuk, Tiyatro Sk. No:25, 16860 İzni̇k/Bursa, Türkiye
sites.summary: Perhaps the site of a once-important church and pilgrimage site from the 13th century
sites.description: The Church of St. Tryphon was built during the reign of Emperor Theodore II Laskaris, it was later destroyed and vanished from history. While some sites are marked on various maps, we do not know where the original church is.

sites.name: The Red Church, Perushtitsa
sites.summary: A large ruin of a 6th century Byzantine church made of solid brick and with fragmentary frescoes
sites.description: This a large, partially preserved late-Roman/early-Byzantine basilica about 15 km southwest of Plovdiv, probably built under Emperor Anastasius I. It is a rare example of solid brick construction from Late Antiquity, the red brick giving it its name. A few frescoes are left in the ruin.

sites.name: Balatlar Church
sites.address: Ada, Kaynak Sk., 57000 Sinop Merkez/Sinop, Türkiye
sites.summary: A layered complex of Roman-Byzantine ruins, including a long-serving Byzantine church
sites.description: A layered complex with its roots in a Roman bath complex, added to thereafter until the 13th century church, which operated up to the population exchanges of 1924. Still being excavated and revealing its secrets, it is not currently open to the public.

sites.name: Tell Madaba West Acropolis
sites.summary: A layered site with a very long history, the Byzantine layer is famous for mosaic pavements and the Madaba Map
sites.description: Madaba, in Jordan, is the great Byzantine "city of mosaics," and the Byzantine layer is the city's golden age: in the 5th–7th centuries Madaba was a prosperous Christian bishopric famous for its mosaic pavements - the Madaba Map and the Church of the Apostles (dated 568) among them.

sites.name: Jerash Archaeological City
sites.summary: An archaeological site with an embarrassment of Byzantine riches
sites.description: At least fifteen Byzantine churches have been found across the ancient city, some clustered (the Cathedral/St. Theodore group; the Three Churches complex) and others out toward the edges. One ticket covers them all.
sites.hours: 8:00–18:30 Mon, Tue, Wed; 8:00–19:00 Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun

sites.name: Byzantine Church, Amman Citadel
sites.summary: The remains of a Byzantine church on the Amman citadel
sites.description: On the Amman Citadel, called Jabal al-Qal'a, between the Roman Temple of Hercules and the 8th-century Umayyad Palace stands a 6th-century Byzantine basilica, dating to around AD 550. Today it is mainly a ruin

sites.name: Basilica di San Saturnino
sites.address: Piazza S. Cosimo, 09127 Cagliari CA, Italy
sites.summary: Destroyed and restored church that is the oldest surviving Christian monument in Sardinia
sites.description: Despite being spoliated, bombed, and restored, this is the oldest surviving Christian monument in Sardinia, built in a Byzantine-Proto-Romanesque style in the 5th–6th century.

sites.name: Church of the Holy Trinity Saccargia
sites.summary: A Pisan Romanesque church whose frescoes have Byzantine DNA
sites.description: While built in the 12th century, this church is is Pisan Romanesque, not Byzantine architecture. However, the frescoes are markedly Byzantine in style, and well-preserved.

sites.name: Basilica of San Gavino
sites.address: Piazza Martiri Turritani, 07046 Porto Torres SS, Italy
sites.summary: A Romanesque church that sits on the remains of Byzantine churches
sites.description: The largest Romanesque church in Sardinia, built in the early 11th century, this sits on the foundations of two previous churches from the Byzantine era in Sardinia

sites.name: Crèsia e Nuraghe de Santa Sarbana
sites.address: Strada Statale 129 Trasversale Sarda, 08017 Silanus NU, Italy
sites.summary: An architecturally Byzantine church with a long history
sites.description: This church is one of the island's most original early-medieval buildings, dating from the late-antique or Byzantine era and rebuilt in the 10th-11th century.

sites.name: Chiesa di Santa Maria Foris Portas
sites.summary: A small church with frescoes that show a link between classical and Byzantine painting
sites.description: In the Castelseprio archaeological park, this small church holds one of the most celebrated early-medieval fresco cycles in Europe, rediscovered in 1944. Its date is hotly contested, but it is agreed to be an important link between classical and Byzantine painting.
sites.hours: 10:00–17:00 Thu, Fri; 10:00–18:00 Sat–Sun; closed Mon, Tue, Wed

sites.name: Cappella di Sant’Aquilino
sites.address: Corso di Porta Ticinese, 35, 20123 Milano MI, Italy
sites.summary: A chapel in the Basilica of San Lorenzo Maggiore, preserving some of the oldest mosaics in the city
sites.description: Attached to the Basilica of San Lorenzo Maggiore, this octagonal chapel is a 4th–5th-century structure that began as an imperial mausoleum, possibly tied to the Theodosian dynasty or Galla Placidia, and it preserves some of the oldest Christian mosaics in the city.

sites.name: Baths of Constantine
sites.address: Rue du Grand Prieuré, 13200 Arles, France
sites.summary: A well-preserved bath complex built during the reign of Constantine
sites.description: A large early-4th-century Roman bath complex on the bank of the Rhône, the best-preserved baths in Arles and once part of an imperial palace known as the Palais Constantin. They were built during the reign of Constantine the Great, who frequently resided at Arles.

sites.name: Fortress of Ohrid
sites.address: 4Q7V+XXR, Sts. Cyril and Methodius, Ohrid, North Macedonia
sites.summary: A layered fortress site used by Romans, Byzantines, and others
sites.description: Used and modified through the Roman and Byzantine centuries, this fortress owes its present form and name to Tsar Samuel of Bulgaria. After Samuel's defeat, the Byzantine emperor Basil II is said to have destroyed it, and Alexios I Komnenos later restored it.

sites.name: Church of Saints Cosmas and Damian (the Smaller Physician Saints)
alternateNames: Црква Мали Свети Врачи - Св. Кузман и Дамјан
sites.summary: A medieval church with recently rediscovered 14th century frescoes
sites.description: Tucked against the town wall just below the church of Sts. Constantine and Helena, this church was built and decorated in the first half of the 14th century, with 14th century frescoes recently rediscovered under mortar.

sites.name: Icon Gallery of Ohrid
sites.summary: This modest-looking museum holds one of the finest collections of Byzantine icons in the world
sites.description: This modest-looking museum holds one of the finest collections of Byzantine icons in the world, especially rich in Palaiologan-Renaissance work, in double-sided processional icons, and in icons with gilded-silver revetments.

sites.name: Church of the Virgin Mary of the Front Gate
sites.summary: A small 14th century church in the old town
sites.description: A small 14th-century church in the Varoš old town oh Ohrid. Thinly-documented, but it belongs to the same 14th century phase of late Byzantine-Serbian building as its neighbors.

sites.name: Church of the Virgin Mary of the Hospital
sites.summary: A tiny 14th-century church in Ohrid's Old Town that served as the women's quarantine chapel, with original frescoes.
sites.description: A tiny 14th-century church in the heart of the Old Town, one of a pair of "hospital" churches. Their function was quarantine, and this was the women's church. It contains 14th century frescoes.

sites.name: Church of Saint Nicholas of the Hospital
sites.summary: A tiny 14th-century church in Ohrid's Old Town that served as the men's quarantine chapel, preserving medieval frescoes.
sites.description: A tiny 14th-century church in the heart of the Old Town, one of a pair of "hospital" churches. Their function was quarantine, and this was the men's church. It preserves medieval frescoes and notable icon.

sites.name: Church of St. Sophia
sites.summary: An important Byzantine-era church with pre-schism wall paintings
sites.description: Dating initially to the 5th-6th century, this church was rebuilt as a domed basilica and painted in the 11th century. Its frescoes are among the finest surviving Byzantine wall paintings anywhere, and because they predate the Great Schism of 1054 they depict saints of both the Eastern and Western traditions.

sites.name: Early Christian Basilica of Manchevci
sites.summary: A partially excavated early Christian basilica whose mosaic floors date to the first half of the 6th century
sites.description: A partially excavated early Christian basilica whose mosaic floors date to the first half of the 6th century.

sites.name: Plaoshnik Archaeological park
sites.address: 4Q7R+483, Kaneo Plaosnik Pateka, Ohrid 6000, North Macedonia
sites.summary: A site with St. Clement's church and the excavations of a monumental early Christian basilica
sites.description: Here St. Clement built his monastery church of St. Panteleimon, and excavations have revealed a monumental early Christian basilica on the scale of that of a much larger city, with a baptistery and mosaic floors

sites.name: Holy Monastery of the Nativity of the Virgin Mary - Kato Panagia
alternateNames: Ιερά Μονή Γενεσίου της Θεοτόκου - Κάτω Παναγιάς
sites.summary: A 13th century Epirote church with fine frescoes and masonry
sites.description: Founded around 1250 by Michael II Komnenos Doukas, Despot of Epirus, one of three churches he founded as penance for marital infidelity towards his wife, St. Theodora. Preserves fine frescoes and masonry.

sites.name: Holy Church of the Virgin Mary of Blacherna
sites.summary: A 13th century church with frescoes, sculptures, marble inlay, and mosaics
sites.description: Founded around 1250 by Michael II Komnenos Doukas, Despot of Epirus, one of three churches he founded as penance for marital infidelity towards his wife, St. Theodora. The burial church of the Komnenos-Doukas rulers of Epirus, it contains frescoes, sculptures, marble inlays, and mosaics.

sites.name: Arta Castle
sites.summary: A 13th century Epirote castle, typical of the military architecture of the age
sites.description: They fortress at the heart of the town, chiefly attributed to Despot Michael II Komnenos Doukas, although certain architectural elements present now are from later.

sites.name: Holy Church of Saint Theodora
sites.summary: The 13th century Epirote church that houses the relics of St. Theodora along with striking frescoes
sites.description: Founded around 1250 by Michael II Komnenos Doukas, Despot of Epirus, one of three churches he founded as penance for marital infidelity towards his wife, St. Theodora, and contains her relics along with striking frescoes.

sites.name: Holy Church of the Virgin Mary Paregoretissa
sites.summary: Architecturally notable medieval Byzantine church with cantilevered columns holding up a mosaiced dome
sites.description: The jewel of Byzantine Arta and its metropolitan church, rebuilt in the late 13th century by Despot Nikephoros I Komnenos Doukas and his wife Anna Palaiologina Kantakouzene. Architecturally notable, with cantilevered columns stacked on projecting brackets, it also contains rich sculpture and mosaic.

sites.name: Church of St. Basil of the Agora
sites.summary: A small, 14th century church with cloisonné masonry and glazed clay icons
sites.description: A small Byzantine church built toward the end of the 14th century with very distinctive brickwork, its surviving wall paintings date to the 17th century.

sites.name: Church of St. George Omorfokklisia
sites.summary: A 12th century church whose nickname "beautiful church" is well-earned by its 13th century wall paintings
sites.description: Built in the second half of the 12th century, over an earlier Christian temple, its walls were painted in the last quarter of the 13th century, and the beauty and range of those frescoes have earned it the nickname "a museum of hagiography."

sites.name: Agios Georgios, Omorfoklisia
sites.summary: A 12th century Byzantine church with a large wooden statue of St. George and medieval frescoes
sites.description: A 12th-century domed cross-in-square Byzantine church, its interior frescoes dating to the 13th and 15th centuries; though damaged under Ottoman rule and by an interior fire, it survives in good condition.

sites.name: Holy Monastery of Saint John Kynegos
alternateNames: Ιερά Μονή Αγίου Ιωάννου του Κυνηγού
sites.summary: A monastery/convent with a middle-Byzantine church
sites.description: A 12th-century domed cross-in-square Byzantine church, its interior frescoes dating to the 13th and 15th centuries; though damaged under Ottoman rule and by an interior fire, it survives in good condition.

sites.name: St. Demetrios Loumbardiaris
sites.summary: A picturesque church at the foot of Philopappou Hill with 16th century meta-Byzantine paintings
sites.description: A picturesque little church of Byzantine origin, restored in 1955 which uncovered 16th century Byzantine-style wall paintings.

sites.name: Agioi Asomatoi
sites.summary: An 11th century church with fragmentary wall paintings and a silver reliquary
sites.description: An 11th-century Byzantine church dedicated to the "Bodiless Ones," i.e. the Archangels, a 1959 restoration revealed wall-painting fragments and a silver reliquary.

sites.name: Temple of Hephaestus
sites.summary: Converted to a church in the 7th century, this Greek temple spent more of its life serving Christianity than Hephaestus.
sites.description: Why is the Temple of Hephaestus the best-preserved Greek temple in Athens? Because it spent most of its life, beginning in the 7th century, as the Byzantine Greek Orthdox church of St. George Akamates. It doesn't look at all Byzantine, but it is an excellent example of survival through reuse.

sites.name: Horologion of Andronikos Cyrrhestes
sites.summary: Conversion to a church and bell tower allowed this ancient clock and weather vane to survive intact
sites.description: Much like the ruins of the Temple of Hephaestus, this edifice survived so well because in the early Christian period the tower was converted into a church or baptistery, then a bell tower, another example of survival through reuse.

sites.name: Holy Monastery of Saint John the Theologian
alternateNames: Ιερά Μονή Αγίου Ιωάννου του Θεολόγου
sites.summary: A minor, lightly documented, but genuine, medieval Byzantine church in the heart of the Plaka
sites.description: This is the small Plaka church of Agios Ioannis Theologos, in the upper old town. It is genuine, from the 11th or perhaps early 12th century, but it is minor and lightly documented.

sites.name: Holy Monastery of Saint John the Theologian
alternateNames: Ιερά Μονή Αγίου Ιωάννου του Θεολόγου
sites.summary: A UNESCO site and pilgrimage destination, this massive monastery was built up in the 11th century
sites.description: One of the great Byzantine monastic foundations, this monastery was founded by imperial edict in 1088 and built over the foundations of a 4th century basilica, itself said to stand on a temple to Artemis. A UNESCO site and a pilgrimage destination.

sites.name: Holy Church of Saint Nicholas Rangavas
sites.summary: The 11th century church whose bell first rang at Athens's liberation, and partially destroyed by a Venetian cannonball
sites.description: A lovely 11th-century Byzantine church high in Plaka, near Anafiotika. During the 1687 Venetian siege of the Acropolis under Morosini, a cannonball destroyed part of the church, and only the northern side and the dome survive from the Byzantine phase. It's traditionally the church whose bell first rang at Athens's liberation.

sites.name: Holy Church of Saint Catherine
sites.summary: A simple 11th century Byzantine structure with weather columns from an ancient Roman temple
sites.description: A simple cross-in-square church with a dome from the 11th century, the wall paintings inside are from the 18th and 19th centuries, making the architecture the most notable Byzantine element. There are, however, the ruins of an ancient Roman temple lying beside the church.

sites.name: Holy Church of the Holy Trinity - Soteira Lykodemos
alternateNames: Ιερός Ναός Αγίας Τριάδος - Σώτειρα Λυκοδήμου
sites.summary: A large, octagonal, 11th century church later rededicated to the Russian Orthodox Church
sites.description: The largest surviving medieval church in Athens, and one of the great octagonal churches of Greece, in the vein of Daphni. Bought by the Russian government in the 19th century and rededicated as Russian Orthodox, leading to its nickname, the "Russian church."
sites.hours: 10:00–14:00 T, Thu, Sat; 16:00–19:00 Thu, Fri; closed Mon, Sun

sites.name: Holy Church of the Virgin Mary Gorgoepikoos and Saint Eleutherius
alternateNames: Ιερός Ναός Παναγίας Γοργοεπηκόου και Αγίου Ελευθερίου
sites.summary: A small church made almost entirely of spolia
sites.description: This small wonder is made almost entirely out of reused ancient marble blocks and reliefs. Over ninety exterior sculpted pieces span classical, Hellenistic, Roman, and earlier Byzantine work.

sites.name: Hadrian's Library
sites.summary: A monument whose courtyard plays host to the remains of multiple Byzantine churches
sites.description: The courtyard of this Roman edifice hosted a stacked sequence of Byzantine churches: a 5th century tetraconch, a 7th century basilica, and another church in the 12th century that burned in the late 1800s.

sites.name: Byzantine and Christian Museum
sites.summary: One of the world's foremost museums of Byzantine art, from early Christianity through the fall and beyond
sites.description: Housed n the 19th-century Villa Ilissia, this is one of the world's foremost museums of Byzantine art, containing objects from the early Christian era through the fall of Constantinople and beyond, covering icons, wall paintings, mosaics, sculpture, manuscripts, ceramics, metalwork, and textiles.

sites.name: Petraki Monastery
alternateNames: The Holy Monastery of the Asomaton Taxiarchon
sites.summary: A working monastery with a 10-11th century katholikon with later-dated art
sites.description: This is a working monastery and the administrative seat of the Archdiocese of Athens. Its katholikon is a middle-Byzantine cross-in-square church generally dated to around the 10th–11th century, making it one of the older churches in the city, with a later dome and 17th-century wall paintings.

sites.name: Manasija
sites.address: Despota Stefana Lazarevića бб, 35213, Despotovac, Serbia
sites.summary: A walled Serbian Orthodox complex whose church contains the final flowering of Byzantine-tradition art in Serbia
sites.description: Sitting inside a massive fortress of eleven towers, this late-medieval Serbian Orthodox monastery was built between 1407 and 1418. Its remaining frescoes represent the peak of Serbian medieval painting.

sites.name: Church of Saint Jovan the Theologian at Kaneo
sites.summary: Iconic clifftop church exemplifies the North Macedonian Byzantine tradition
sites.description: Utterly iconic clifftop church, and the most photographed building in the country, this UNESCO site is dedicated to St. John the Theologian. Restoration in 1964 uncovered its medieval wall painting.

sites.name: Church of the Virgin Mary Peribleptos
sites.summary: A late-13th century church with wall paintings by two of the greatest artists of the age
sites.description: This church stands in the old Varoš of Ohrid, and it was completed in 1295, just after the Byzantines recovered Ohrid in 1290. Its late-13th century wall paintings are absolutely masterful
sites.hours: 9:00–14:00 Mon; 9:00–16:00 Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri; closed Sat–Sun

sites.name: Panagia tou Araka
alternateNames: Monastery of the Virgin Mary of Arakas
sites.summary: A church containing the most complete cycle of late-Komnenian painting in Cyprus
sites.description: This UNESCO-listed church is one of the best examples of the art of the period, given almost nothing contemporaneous survived the Fourth Crusade in Constantinople. The frescoes are the most complete cycle of late-Komnenian painting on the island, executed by the Constantinople-trained monk Theodoros Apsevdis.

sites.name: Agios Nikolaos tis Stegis
sites.summary: An 11th century monastery church, fully painted inside with layered art
sites.description: The sole surviving building of an 11th century monastery, the inside of the steep-roofed church is fully painted, with layers spanning the 11th through the 17th century, including a celebrated Forty Martyrs and a fine St. Nicholas.

sites.name: Agios Sozomenos Church
sites.address: XVWX+H8H, Hall Pass, Galata, Lefkosia 2827, Cyprus
sites.summary: A small post-Byzantine church painted by Symeon Axentis
sites.description: A small, post-Byzantine painted church whose donors' names are inscribed. The paintings are early works of the painter Symeon Axentis, in a more traditional Byzantine idiom with only light Western influence.

sites.name: Panagia tou Moutoulla
sites.summary: A painted chapel that melds Byzantine and Crusader/Italian influence
sites.description: A tiny chapel built and painted in 1280, with a narthex added after 1500. Its frescoes capture the meeting of continued Byzantine tradition and Crusader and Italian influence, sitting as they do in the early Lusignan period.

sites.name: Archangelos Michail
sites.summary: A late-15th century painted church showing a blend of influences
sites.description: Built and frescoed in 1474, this is a small, steep-roofed UNESCO church whose late-15th-century wall paintings show the harmonious blend of Byzantine tradition, local Cypriot idiom, and touches of Western influence.

sites.name: Byzantine Museum of Pedoulas
sites.summary: A small, village museum with icons and objects from the Marathasa valley
sites.description: A small ecclesiastical museum in Pedoulas, housed near the parish church, displaying icons and liturgical objects gathered from the churches of the Marathasa valley, from the 13th to the 20th century.

sites.name: Church of the Holy Cross
sites.summary: A 14th century church with notable Palaiologan period wall paintings
sites.description: Once the property of Jean de Lusignan, son of King Hugh IV, this 14th-century church is one of the UNESCO ten, notable for wall paintings of the Palaiologan period that show the revived art of late-Byzantine Constantinople alongside local and Western elements.

sites.name: Panagias Katholikis
sites.summary: An interesting contrast to its Palaiologan neighbor, this post-Byzantine church shows more of an Italo-Byzantine style
sites.description: This church dates to the early 16th century, with wall paintings in the Italo-Byzantine style that flourished on Cyprus under Venetian rule, marrying Byzantine iconography with Italian Renaissance forms.

sites.name: Timios Stavros Monastery
sites.address: RRX5+3F9, Timios Stavros Square, Omodos, Lemesos 4760, Cyprus
sites.summary: An old and traditional monastery long associated with relics of the Holy Cross
