sites.description: One of the oldest and best-known monasteries on the island, traditionally said to predate the Byzantine period and long associated with relics of the Holy Cross. The present buildings are largely 18th and 19th century.

sites.name: Church of Panagia Katholiki (Panagia Odigitria)
sites.summary: A medieval Byzantine church with 15th century wall painting next to a famous Sanctuary of Aphrodite
sites.description: The Church of Panagia Katholiki is situated just next to the famous Sanctuary of Aphrodite in Palaia Paphos. It was constructed during the 12th-13th century, with additions in the 16th century. The church is decorated with 15th century wall painting.

sites.name: Church of the Virgin Mary of Podithou
sites.summary: Byzantine tradition meets the Latin West in this Venetian-influenced UNESCO church
sites.description: Built in 1502, this UNESCO church has frescoes that are a leading example of the Italo-Byzantine style: the iconography remains Orthodox, but the modeling, architecture, and details are strongly Italian-Renaissance.

sites.name: Archangelos Michael Chapel
sites.summary: A small chapel completely painted in the post-Byzantine style
sites.description: This small chapel is completely painted in the post-Byzantine style and belongs to Galata's cluster of four painted churches.

sites.name: Panagia Theotokos
sites.summary: A small, 16th century painted church in Kakopetria
sites.description: A small 16th-century church whose painter probably also did the nearby Archangelos Michael Chapel, this roughly half of its murals.

sites.name: Agia Paraskevi Church
sites.address: XWV2+7PR, Makariou III Ave, Galata, Nicosia 2827, Cyprus
sites.summary: A small, 16th century painted church in Galata
sites.description: A small church on the old Kakopetria–Galata road, with murals dating to 1514. Post-Byzantine, like its neighbors.

sites.name: Agios Georgios Perachoritis Church
sites.summary: A small, 16th century painted church in Kakopetria
sites.description: This small church has original wall paintings from the first quarter of the 16th century, of some originality.

sites.name: Monastery of Saint John Lampadistes
alternateNames: Ιερά Μονή Αγίου Ιωάννου του Λαμπαδιστού
sites.summary: A layered and well-preserved monastic complex with art and architecture from the 11th to the 16th centuries
sites.description: A beautifully preserved, UNESCO-listed, monastic complex, which is actually a composite of churches under one huge timber roof: an 11th century church of Agios Irakleidios, a 12th century church with St. John Lampadistes' remains, and a 13th century Italo-Byzantine chapel. Contains Palaiologan and Italo-Byzantine paintings.

sites.name: Panagia Phorviotissa tis Asinou
sites.summary: One of the crown jewels of Byzantine Cyprus, with a complete sequence of Byzantine wall painting
sites.description: One of the crown jewels of Byzantine Cyprus, this small, barn-roofed 12th-century church that was the katholikon of the vanished monastery "of the Phorbia." It preserves one of the most complete sequences of Byzantine wall painting in the Mediterranean, built up from the early 12th to the 17th century.

sites.name: Church of the Holy Cross of Agiasmati at Platanistasa
alternateNames: Ιερός Ναός Τιμίου Σταυρού του Αγιασμάτι
sites.summary: One of the best cycles of 15th century wall painting on the island
sites.description: This 15th-century painted church holds the most complete cycle of later-15th-century wall painting on the island. The frescoes, completed in 1494 and signed by the important painter Philippos Goul, are unusually rich on the theme of the Cross.

sites.name: Metamorphosis tou Sotiros
alternateNames: Church of the Transfiguration of the Saviour
sites.summary: a post-Byzantine UNESCO site with a melding of Palaiologan and Western Renaissance styles
sites.description: An early-16th-century chapel on the slope above Palaichori village, and one of the ten UNESCO-listed painted churches, this church is completely covered with one of the most complete series of murals of the post-Byzantine period in Cyprus. Palaiologan and Western Renaissance elements abound.

sites.name: Panagia Crysopantanassa
sites.summary: A post-Byzantine church with unique wall paintings
sites.description: A 16th-century gabled, timber-roofed church, with wall paintings dating to the same century. Among its frescoes is a rare image: Saints Demetrios and George depicted together on horseback, the only one of its kind in Cyprus.

sites.name: Ss. Paraskevi and Christina
sites.summary: A 16th century chapel with notable post-Byzantine art
sites.description: An open, country chapel about 2 km outside Fterikoudi, clad in irregular local stone and housing notable post-Byzantine frescoes concentrated in the sanctuary.

sites.name: Holy Monastery of Panagia Machaira
sites.summary: An important working monastery with its roots in the 12th century
sites.description: This working monastery in the Troodos grew around the legendary discovery of an icon painted by St. Luke, and through Komnenian patronage. The present buildings were rebuilt after fires, but the complex holds important manuscripts, icons, and relics.

sites.name: Monastery of the Virgin Mary Chrysokourdaliotissa
sites.summary: A 16th century monastery church with Italo-Byzantine art
sites.description: This church dates to the 16th century, built as a monastery katholikon, and is a timber-roofed church noted for its wall paintings and fine carved-wood iconostasis in the Italo-Byzantine idiom of Venetian-era Cyprus.

sites.name: Holy Monastery of the Virgin Mary of Kykkos
sites.summary: A monastery and museum with roots in the 11th century and a Lukan icon
sites.description: The most famous and wealthy monastery in Cyprus, founded at the end of the 11th century under Emperor Alexios I Komnenos. It contains the icon of Panagia Kykkotissa, one of the three icons traditionally attributed to the Apostle Luke, kept perpetually veiled in a silver-gilt cover before the iconostasis. Its rebuilt modern buildings house a superb museum.

sites.name: Chrysoroyiatissa Monastery
sites.address: WJ59+XF6, E703, Pano Panagia, Pafos 8640, Cyprus
sites.summary: Monastery and winery with a significant collection of Byzantine treasures
sites.description: Founded in the 12th century, the present buildings date largely from around 1770, and it holds a significant collection of icons and treasures, plus (in modern times) a monastery winery.

sites.name: Trooditissa Monastery
sites.summary: A working monastery of the western mountains, tracings its roots back to the 8th century
sites.description: A monastery whose tradition traces to an 8th-century icon of the Virgin hidden in a cave during the Iconoclast persecutions. The present church and buildings are, however, largely 18th-century and later, having been rebuilt after fires.

sites.name: Stavrovouni Monastery
sites.summary: Traditionally the oldest monastery in Cyprus, with 20th century wall paintings by one of its monks, a renowned painter of the Byzantine tradition.
sites.description: Traditionally the oldest monastery in Cyprus, said to have been founded around 327–330 by St. Helena, who left a piece of the True Cross there, which is still its central relic. Ottomans destroyed much of the original complex, so its buildings are later, and its paintings are 20th century (by Kallinikos Stavrovouniotis), though still firmly within the Byzantine tradition.

sites.name: Church of the Archangel Michael
sites.summary: A surviving monastery church from the 12th century, with a set of notable frescoes
sites.description: This is the surviving church of the vanished Monastery of the Asomatos, built of local fieldstone, containing a limited but very important set of 12th-century frescoes, including a notable Holy Mandylion.

sites.name: Church of St. Anthony
alternateNames: Historical Holy Church of St. Anthony
sites.address: Agios Antonios Church, Kellia, Larnaka 7503, Cyprus
sites.summary: A rare stratified record of Byzantine fresco across four centuries survives in this 9th century church
sites.description: One of the most important Byzantine churches in Cyprus, it's a three-aisled vaulted basilica with wall paintings in successive layers from the 9th, 11th, and 13th centuries.

sites.name: Church of Saint Lazarus
sites.address: Πλατεία, Ayiou Lazarou, Larnaca, Larnaka 6020, Cyprus
sites.summary: A landmark church over the tomb of Lazarus of Bethany, with adjoining Byzantine museum
sites.description: A landmark of Byzantine Cyprus, over the tomb of Lazarus of Bethany, the domes and bell tower were lost under the Ottomans, and it was converted to a Catholic church under Frankish rule, but the tomb remains and a Byzantine museum adjoins.

sites.name: Limassol Castle
sites.summary: A medieval castle taken from Isaac Komnenos by Richard the Lionheart in the Third Crusade
sites.description: A medieval castle in the old town of Limassol, traditionally famous as the place where Richard the Lionheart married Berengaria in 1191, right after he seized Cyprus from its Byzantine ruler Isaac Komnenos. The present structure is later, from the Lusignan and Ottoman periods.

sites.name: Church of St. Theodosius
sites.summary: A stone-built 13th century church with paintings from the end of Byzantine rule of Cyprus
sites.description: This is a stone-built Byzantine structure with wall paintings inside, dated to the end of the 12th and the beginning of the 13th century, including a donor portrait and lovely depiction of Ss. Peter and Paul.

sites.name: Church of Panagia of Sintis
sites.summary: A recently restored 16th century Veneto-Byzantine church in a dramatic setting
sites.description: The monastery church of Panagia tou Sinti, this is a fine 16th-century monastery church, single-aisled and domed, and one of the shining examples of Veneto-Byzantine architecture. A careful restoration in the 1990s brought it back from abandonment.

sites.name: Church of St Kirikos and Ioulitti
alternateNames: Ιερός Ναός Αγίων Κηρύκου και Ιουλίττης
sites.summary: A 12th century church with layered wall painting from the 12th to the 15th centuries
sites.description: A 12th-century cross-in-square domed church with later frescoes, especially from the 15th century. As of this writing, it is closed for restoration.

sites.name: Monastery of Saint Neophytos
alternateNames: Ιερά Μονή Αγίου Νεοφύτου του Εγκλείστου
sites.address: RCWW+7P2 Ιερά Μονή Αγίου Νεοφύτου, Agios Neofytos Ave., Tala, Pafos 8576, Cyprus
sites.summary: A remarkable rock-cut monastery with valuable 12 century painting
sites.description: A remarkable monastery founded by St. Neophytos the Recluse in 1159, who carved its Enkleistra by hand into the cliff face, then had decorated with superb frescoes, including some by Theodoros Apsevdis, the Constantinopolitan master who painted in Lagoudera.

sites.name: Agios Georgios Church
sites.address: W839+3VF, Agiou Georgiou, Άγιος Γεώργιος, Pafos 8570, Cyprus
sites.summary: A Neo-Byzantine church standing aside the ruins of a bustling 6th century port town destroyed by Muslims
sites.description: Excavations at this site have revealed three 6th-century basilicas with fine mosaic floors, tombs, an episcopal complex, baths, and a harbor, ultimately destroyed by Muslim Arab raiders. The modern Byzantine-style church of St. George stands beside the ruins.

sites.name: Panagia Chryseleousa
sites.summary: A church built in stages with paintings spanning centuries
sites.description: Structurally a fusion of two churches, eastern section built in the 12th century and western in the 13th, it preserves valuable wall paintings spanning the 12th, 13th, 15th, and 16th centuries and a fine iconostasis.

sites.name: Agios Georgios Church
sites.summary: A minor, lightly documented parish church of Byzantine/post-Byzantine character
sites.description: A minor, lightly documented parish church of Byzantine/post-Byzantine character.

sites.name: Agia Solomoni Catacomb
sites.address: Apostolou Pavlou Ave 100, Paphos, Pafos 8042, Cyprus
sites.summary: A rock-cut tomb complex with 12th century fragmentary frescoes
sites.description: An underground rock-cut tomb complex, several chambers preserve fragmentary frescoes of Christian saints, generally dated to the 12th century with some even earlier phases.

sites.name: Church of Agia Paraskevi
sites.summary: A unique five-domed basilica with painting from the 9th, 12th, and 15th centuries
sites.description: Famous for its unusual form: a five-domed basilica, and the only remaining example of this kind on the island. Its thick walls carry layered frescoes: fragments from the 9th century, including iconoclastic non-figural decorations, over which lie 12th-century and, most extensively, 15th-century painting.

sites.name: Paphos Castle
sites.address: Kato Paphos Harbour, Coastal Broadwalk, Paphos, Pafos 8040, Cyprus
sites.summary: A harbor castle of Ottoman over Frankish over Byzantine foundations
sites.description: Originally a Byzantine fort built to protect the harbor, it was rebuilt by the Lusignans in the 13th century, destroyed by the Venetians in 1570 to deny it to the Ottomans, and rebuilt again in the Ottoman 16th century.

sites.name: Agia Kyriaki Chrysopolitissa
sites.address: QC57+5M4, Panagias Theoskepastis, Paphos, Pafos 8041, Cyprus
sites.summary: A 13th century church standing among the ruins of a 4th century complex with extant floor mosaics, where St. Paul was said to be flogged
sites.description: The medieval church sits amid the excavated ruins of the largest Early Byzantine basilica on the island: the Chrysopolitissa basilica, built at the end of the 4th century as the cathedral of Paphos. In the compound stands St. Paul's Pillar, where tradition holds that Paul was lashed until the Roman governor converted.

sites.name: Church of Panagia Theoskepasti
sites.address: QC48+R7V, Panagias Theoskepastis, Paphos, Pafos 8041, Cyprus
sites.summary: The reconstruction of an earlier church with a venerated icon
sites.description: There has been a church on this spot since the Byzantine period, but the present building is 20th-century, although it holds a venerated, silver-clad icon said to be by St. Luke.

sites.name: Church of the Virgin Mary Angeloktisti
sites.summary: A partially late-antique, partially Byzantine church with a magnificent 6th century apse mosaic
sites.description: The present domed, cross-in-square church was built in the 11th century over the ruins of a 5th-century early Christian basilica, whose apse holds a 6th century wall mosaic, among the finest works of Justinianic mosaic anywhere. Currently on the UNESCO tentative list.

sites.name: Antiphonitis church
sites.summary: A story of modern looting and smuggling, the frescoes of this late-Byzantine church now lie elsewhere
sites.description: A late Byzantine church with 12th and 15th-16th century frescoes that were stripped off and looted after the Turkish invasion of 1974. A sordid saga of sale, smuggling, arrest, and repatriation has brought the art back to the Byzantine Museum of Nicosia, but the church remains here, barren.

sites.name: Panaghia Kanakaria Monastery
sites.summary: A story of modern looting and smuggling, the 6th century mosaics of this late-Byzantine church survived iconoclasm intact, but were stolen in the 1970s
sites.description: An early church with 6th century apse mosaics, among the very few Early Byzantine mosaics to survive the Iconoclasm of the 8th–9th centuries, which were then looted by Turkish occupiers in 1979, only to be repatriated when an art dealer tried to sell them to the Getty Museum in Los Angeles. Mosaics now in a museum, the church lies bare.

sites.name: Monastery of Saint Barnabas
alternateNames: St. Barnabas Arkeoloji ve İkon Müzesi
sites.summary: A key shrine in early Cypriot Christianity, now with a later church serving as icon museum
sites.description: The original shrine was founded in the late 5th century by Emperor Zeno, in honor of the Apostle Barnabas, evangelizer of Cyprus, whose tomb lies here. The present, 18th century church serves as an icon and archaeological museum.

sites.name: Saint Hilarion Castle
sites.summary: A mountain fortress whose ruined monastic church sits over the tomb of St. Hilarion
sites.description: A spectacular mountain fortress commanding the pass to Nicosia, it began as a hermitage of the monk Hilarion, and by the 10th century the Byzantines had built a church and monastery over his tomb. From the 11th century they fortified the site.

sites.name: Church of Saints Barnabas and Hilarion
alternateNames: Ιερός Ναός Οσίων Βαρνάβα και Ιλαρίωνος
sites.summary: A five-dome church with post-Byzantine wall paintings
sites.description: Once one of the finest examples of Cypriot Byzantine architecture: a rare five-domed church. Only part of the original north wall survives, but the church was reconstructed on the five-dome plan, and its oldest wall paintings are 15th–16th century.

sites.name: The Cyprus Museum
sites.summary: A noted archaeological museum
sites.description: The island's principal and oldest archaeological museum, noted mainly for its pre-Byzantine finds, but worth a look for its Roman and antique collections.

sites.name: Aphendrika
sites.summary: Three ruined Byzantine churches stand here amid a deserted classical city
sites.description: The scattered ruins of the ancient city of Ourania/Aphendrika, containing three ruined churches that stand close together: Panagia Chrysiotissa (6th century); Agios Georgios (10th century); and Panagia Asomatos (unknown).

sites.name: Byzantine Museum
alternateNames: Βυζαντινό Μουσείο και Πινακοθήκη του Ιδρύματος Αρχιεπισκόπου Μακαρίου Γ΄
sites.address: Πλ. Αρχιεπισκόπου Κυπριανού, Nicosia, Lefkosia 1016, Cyprus
sites.summary: The most important collection of Byzantine art and artifacts on the island
sites.description: The most important collection of Byzantine art on the island, it holds around 230 icons spanning the 8th to the 19th century, frescoes, mosaics, and liturgical objects. Crucially, it's where the repatriated looted treasures now live.

sites.name: Agios Philon Agridion Church
sites.summary: A Cypriot Romanesque church that sits atop a Roman basilica whose mosaic floors survive
sites.description: This one of the rare Cypriot churches built in a Romanesque rather than Byzantine idiom, and it sits atop the ruins of larger 4th–5th-century early Christian episcopal basilica with geometric mosaic floors.

sites.name: Hagia Nikola Church
sites.summary: A small church, enlarged and rebuilt in the Gothic style later on, only to be converted to a cloth market
sites.description: This building's core is a small Byzantine church, generally traced to around the 12th century, dedicated to St. Nicholas. Under Lusignan and then Venetian rule it was massively enlarged and rebuilt in Gothic style, becoming a substantial church. Following the Ottoman invasion it became a cloth market.

sites.name: Basilica of Agias Triadas
sites.summary: A recently-restored early Christian basilica with an extensive, geometric mosaic floor
sites.description: These ruins of a large 5th–6th-century early Christian basilica were excavated in 1935–38 and named for the Holy Trinity. Its glory is an extensive geometric mosaic floor, among the finest early-Byzantine pavements on the island. It was destroyed by Arabs and only recently restored.

sites.name: Agios Synesios
sites.summary: A 12th century church, one of the few remaining living churches in the occupied Karpas
sites.description: A Byzantine-origin church, generally dated around the 12th century with later phases, it's one of only a handful of churches in the north where the remaining Greek Orthodox residents are permitted to hold regular liturgies.

sites.name: Agios Thrysos
sites.summary: The crypt of an early church here stands atop a holy spring
sites.description: Two churches stand here, a late upper church, and an early lower church standing atop a sacred spring (ayiasma) said to have healing powers, reached by steps down to the water's edge.

sites.name: Heraclea Lyncestis
sites.summary: A site containing two early Christian basilicas and early floor mosaics
sites.description: Founded by Philip II of Macedon around 350 BC and prosperous on the Via Egnatia under Rome, Heraclea became an early Byzantine episcopal center. The remains of two early Christian basilicas contain notable floor mosaics.

sites.name: Holy Church of Saints Theodores
sites.summary: A fine 11th century Byzantine church in the heart of Athens
sites.description: A fine 11th-century Byzantine church in the heart of Athens. It was built partly over a Roman mansion, with the cloisonné masonry and brick ornament typical of middle-Byzantine Athens.

sites.name: Holy Church of the Holy Apostles of Solakis
alternateNames: Ιερός Ναός Αγίων Αποστόλων του Σολάκη
sites.summary: The only medieval monument to survive in the Agora, and among Athens's oldest churches
sites.description: The only medieval monument to survive in the Agora, and one of the oldest churches in Athens, built around the late 10th century. Carefully restored by the American School in the 1950s, who brought in surviving frescoes from the demolished nearby church of Agios Spyridon.

sites.name: Church of the Virgin Mary Pantanassa - Monastiraki
sites.summary: An iconic church in the heart of Athens, dating from the 11th century
sites.description: The church that gives Monastiraki its name, it's one of the oldest churches in Athens, with datings ranging (depending on the scholar) from the 10th to the 12th century. The bell tower, frescoes, and iconography are later additions.

sites.name: Anavatos
sites.summary: A ghost town emptied by a massacre in the Greek War of Independence, this site contains medieval churches, chapels, and fortifications
sites.description: A dramatic, near-abandoned medieval "ghost village" on a steep cliff in central Chios, sometimes called the "Mystras of the Aegean," largely emptied after the Ottoman massacre. Its Byzantine layer includes the church of the Taxiarchis and other small chapels.

sites.name: Koimisis tis Theotokou
alternateNames: Ιερός Ναός Κοιμήσεως της Θεοτόκου Έδεσσας
sites.summary: A 12th century Byzantine church with spolia and frescoes
sites.description: This is a 12th-century three-aisled basilica that reuses impressive ancient columns and spolia and preserves fragmentary frescoes.

sites.name: Byzantine walls of Drama
sites.summary: Layered Byzantine walls of the old city of Drama
sites.description: Drama preserves stretches of its Byzantine fortification walls in the old town, around the area of the Agia Sophia church and the archaeological core.

sites.name: Hagia Sophia Drama
sites.summary: A 10th century middle Byzantine church, much restored
sites.description: The principal Byzantine monument of Drama's old town, usually dated to the 10th century. Much restored and altered, and echoing in miniature the great Hagia Sophias of Constantinople, Thessalonica, and Ohrid.

sites.name: Basilica of Saint Achillius
sites.summary: The ruin of a 10th century church built to house the relics of St. Achillius, taken in the capture of Larissa
sites.description: One of the most historically charged Byzantine ruins in Greece. It's a large three-aisled, wooden-roofed basilica with a narthex, built at the end of the 10th century by Tsar Samuel of Bulgaria. The roofless ruin, with its row of arches reflected in the lake, is the most important monument in the Prespa lakes.

sites.name: Monastery of the Virgin Mary Porphyra
sites.summary: A post-Byzantine monastery in Lake Prespa
sites.description: A small post-Byzantine monastery in Lake Prespa, in the Byzantine tradition. Its annual festival, held around the November feast of the Virgin, is famous for participants dressing in authentic traditional costume.

sites.name: Basilica of the Twelve Apostles
sites.summary: A small, ruined church dated to the 11th-12th century
sites.description: One of the small scattered churches on Agios Achillios island, dated to the 11th–12th century, contemporary with or just after Samuel's great basilica.

sites.name: Church of St. John the Baptist
sites.summary: A layered church whose current edifice dates to the 11th century and is said to be where the head of St. John the Baptist lay
sites.description: A layered church, the above-ground edifice dates mostly to the 11th century, but its crypt is Late Roman or Byzantine (c. 324–500). This is where Amalfitan merchants built a pilgrim hospice that became the germ of the Knights Hospitaller in the Crusades. Byzantine sources place a shrine holding the Baptist's head here.

sites.name: Church of St. Peter in Gallicantu
sites.summary: The site of St. Peter's denial, and originally of a Byzantine basilica, still containing 5th century mosaics
sites.description: This church marks the traditional site of the house of the high priest Caiaphas, where St. Peter denied Jesus three times. The first church here was a Byzantine basilica/shrine, built around 457–460, likely under the patronage of the Empress Eudocia. Two 5th-century Byzantine floor mosaics from the original shrine survive.

sites.name: Pool of Siloam
sites.summary: The site of Empress Eudocia's church over the presumed pool of Siloam of John, Chapter 9
sites.description: The pool is famous from John 9, where Jesus heals the man born blind by sending him to wash there, and for roughly 1,500 years, the pool that pilgrims venerated as the Pool of Siloam was a Byzantine one: in the 5th century (around 440), the Empress Eudocia remodeled a pool and built a church over it. The actual pool was accidentally discovered in 2004 about 50 meters away.

sites.name: Holy Church of Saint Demetrius
alternateNames: Ιερός Ναός Αγίου Δημητρίου, Πολιούχου Θεσσαλονίκης
sites.summary: An extremely important Byzantine site with relics, pre-Iconoclasm mosaics, and frescoes
sites.description: The present basilica took its form after fires and earthquakes, largely rebuilt around 500 and again in the 7th century, over the remains of St. Demetrius. Its supreme treasure is the set of votive mosaic panels of the 5th–7th centuries, the finest surviving pre-Iconoclasm Byzantine portraits. Later frescoes include a scene tied to the 14th-century Hesychast controversy.

sites.name: Heptapyrgion of Thessaloniki
sites.summary: A layered Byzantine fortification crowning the Thessaloniki citadel
sites.description: The core of this fortification is Byzantine: the northern towers and walls go back to the late 4th/early 5th century (under Theodosius I), the southern towers and inner keep are likely 12th-century, and the last Byzantine additions came under the Palaiologoi in 1369–1373 (Manuel II).

sites.name: Virgin Mary Gorgoepikoos
alternateNames: Ιερός Ναός Παναγούδας (Γενεσίου της Θεοτόκου) - Γοργοϋπήκοος
sites.summary: A rebuilt church in the center of Thessaloniki housing a venerated icon
sites.description: A church in the center of Thessaloniki dedicated to the Virgin Gorgoepikoos ("she who is quick to hear/answer"), rebuilt after a 19th century fire, housing a much-venerated icon of the Panagia Gorgoepikoos.

sites.name: Holy Church of Saint Panteleimon
sites.address: Λεωνίδα Ιασωνίδου, Αρριανού, Arrianou &, Thessaloniki 546 35, Greece
sites.summary: An architectural gem of a church with 14th century wall paintings
sites.description: A jewel of late-Byzantine architecture in the upper town, built between the late 13th and early 14th century, this domed church preserves Palaiologan wall paintings.

sites.name: Latomos Monastery - Holy Church of Hosios David
alternateNames: Ιερά Μονή Λατόμου - Ιερός Ναός Οσίου Δαβίδ
sites.summary: A small church containing an extraordinary and unique pre-Iconoclasm mosaic and 12th century frescoes
sites.description: Small, unassuming, and holding one of the most extraordinary mosaics in all of Byzantine art. The old katholikon of the Latomou Monastery contains a unique, pre-Iconoclasm early mosaic of the Vision of Ezekiel. The church also preserves fine 12th-century frescoes.

sites.name: Church of the Transfiguration of the Savior
sites.address: Παλαιών Πατρών Γερμανού, Egnatia 138, Thessaloniki 546 22, Greece
sites.summary: An elegant church with Palaiologan frescoes
sites.description: A small but elegant late-Byzantine church of the early 14th century, partly sunk below the modern street level. The church preserves early-14th-century frescoes in the dome and elsewhere, in the refined Palaiologan manner.

sites.name: Tower of Prosphorion
sites.summary: A medieval stone tower housing a museum of Athos-area finds
sites.description: The great stone tower dominating the little harbor of Ouranoupoli, first attested in the 14th century, but perhaps older. Inside, its floors now house a museum of Byzantine and archaeological finds from Athos-area sites

sites.name: Holy Monastery of Hosios Loukas
sites.summary: An extremely important Middle Byzantine site with a complete cycle of 11th century mosaics
sites.description: One of the supreme monuments of Middle Byzantine art, the great katholikon rose in the first half of the 11th century over the tomb of Loukas the Steiriote. It preserves reserves one of the most complete surviving programs of early-11th-century Byzantine mosaics.

sites.name: Kavala Fortress
sites.summary: A fortress rebuilt over a Byzantine foundation
sites.description: The acropolis of Kavala was fortified in the Byzantine period, but what stands today is mostly Ottoman, rebuilt over the Byzantine circuit.

sites.name: Gračanica Monastery
sites.summary: A masterpiece of Serbo-Byzantine art and architecture
sites.description: A masterpiece of late-Byzantine architecture and of the Serbo-Byzantine style with 14th century frescoes and a painted dynastic genealogy, still an active convent.

sites.name: Church of the Virgin of Ljeviš
sites.summary: A 14th century Serbian church with Palaiologan revival frescoes, damaged in recent riots
sites.description: A Serbian Orthodox church in Prizren, consecrated around 1307 under King Milutin, who converted and rebuilt an earlier Byzantine structure and added its interior program. Its early-14th-century frescoes are among the important monuments of the Palaiologan revival in Serbia. Attacked and burned during anti-Serb riots in 2004, and under restoration since.

sites.name: Patriarchate of Peć
sites.summary: An architecturally unique medieval Serbo-Byzantine site with period frescoes
sites.description: The historic spiritual seat of the Serbian Orthodox Church, it is architecturally unique: four churches fused into one complex under a shared outer narthex. Its component churches and frescoes date from the 13th and 14th centuries.

sites.name: Monastery of Visoki Dečani
sites.summary: A large medieval church containing the largest surviving Byzantine cycle of painting in the world
sites.description: The largest and best-preserved medieval church in the Balkans, fusing Romanesque and Gothic portals and vaults with a Byzantine interior. Its supreme treasure is the fresco program: over 1,000 preserved frescoes, several thousand individual figures, the largest surviving Byzantine cycle anywhere.

sites.name: Chiesa di Santa Maria Antiqua
sites.address: 00186 Rome, Metropolitan City of Rome Capital, Italy
sites.summary: A Roman Forum church with intermittent public access that holds a palimpsest wall and pre-Iconoclasm frescoes
sites.description: One of the two surviving early churches in the Roman Forum, built in the 6th century inside an earlier Roman structure. Covered by an earthquake and subsequent landslide in 847, which thankfully preserved its frescoes until the 20th century. It's palimpsest wall and pre-Iconoclasm frescos are must-see.

sites.name: Arch of Malborghetto
sites.summary: A Roman arch built under Constantine and incorporated into a church in the 11th century
sites.description: A Roman arch built under Constantine, which became a church in the 11th century, thought to mark Constantine's campsite before the Battle of the Milvian Bridge.

sites.name: Villaggio Bizantino
sites.address: Casa del Mastro, Contrada, 94010 Calascibetta EN, Italy
sites.summary: A rock-cut settlement with two-story rock-cut churches, perhaps dating to the time of Belisarius
sites.description: This rock-cut settlement with two two-story rock-cut churches and over thirty caves once used as dwellings, stables, and stores. Local tradition ties it to the Byzantine reconquest of Sicily under Belisarius beginning in 535, but it may be much older.

sites.name: Milazzo Castle
sites.summary: A later castle that sits atop a Byzantine layer
sites.description: The visible castle is Norman–Swabian–Aragonese–Spanish, but there's a real, if buried, Byzantine phase, mostly destroyed by Arabs in the 9th century. Byzantine coins have been found on site.

sites.name: Holy Monastery of Daphni
sites.summary: A UNESCO-listed monastery with archetypal Middle-Byzantine architecture, and one of the most famous Pantokrator mosaics in the world
sites.description: A monastery built on the site of a sanctuary of Apollo, reusing elements of the ancient temple. The present katholikon dates to the late 11th century, and its dome mosaic of Christ Pantokrator is among the most famous images in Byzantine art.

sites.name: Macedonian Tower
sites.address: Çavuşbey, Mumcular Sk. No:9, 22020 Edirne Merkez/Edirne, Türkiye
sites.summary: A Roman, then Byzantine, city fortification series with a Byzantine brick inscription
sites.description: The fortifications began as Hadrian's Roman walls; a second line and defensive tower are Byzantine, from the 10th century, per inscriptions, raised against Bulgarian attacks. The tower carries a fragmentary Byzantine brick inscription of Emperor John I Tzimiskes.

sites.name: Ancient Christian Church of Virgin Mary
sites.summary: A council church inside the archaeological site of Ephesus
sites.description: This church is inside the Ephesus archaeological site. It's the "Council Church," believed to have hosted the Council of Ephesus in 431, establishing Mary as the mother of God. Roman, early Christian, and Byzantine layers.

sites.name: Basilica of Saint John
sites.address: Atatürk, St. Jean Cd. No:4, 35920 Selçuk/İzmir, Türkiye
sites.summary: A great Justinianic church over the tomb of St. John the Evangelist, now ruined
sites.description: A great cruciform, six-domed church built by Justinian in the 6th century over the believed tomb of St. John the Evangelist, its nave capitals bearing the monograms of Justinian and Theodora. Converted to a mosque before earthquakes ruined it.

sites.name: Tomb of Osman Gazi
sites.address: Osmangazi, Yiğitler Cd. No:4, 16040 Osmangazi̇/Bursa, Türkiye
sites.summary: A former Byzantine chapel, now the tombs of the founders of the Ottoman empire, with extant mosaic flooring
sites.description: The tomb of Osman I is a former Byzantine chapel the Ottomans called the Silver Dome; its lead dome glinted like silver during the conquest. Right beside it, the adjoining tomb of his son Orhan encloses the surviving Byzantine mosaic floor of the monastery church.

sites.name: Imperial Gate
alternateNames: Saltanat Kapısı Sini Saltanat Tesisleri Bursa
sites.address: Osmangazi Mahallesi, 16020, Osmangazi, 2. Osman Gazi Cd. No:22, 16040 Osmangazi̇/Bursa, Türkiye
sites.summary: A modern reconstruction of the major gate of the Roman/Byzantine walls
sites.description: The most important gate on the city walls, used by nobles and governors to enter the citadel, an inscription records renovation in 1418 by Sultan Mehmed I. This is largely a modern reconstruction due to 19th century earthquakes.

sites.name: The Gate of Conquest
sites.summary: A renovated gate notable for the conquest of Prousa
sites.description: The southernmost gate of the Roman/Byzantine citadel, at the walls' weakest point opening onto the plain, where Ottoman forces entered Prousa during the 1326 conquest; it was renovated in 2008.

sites.name: Eski Kaplıca Hamamı
sites.address: Kükürtlü, Eski Kaplıca Sk. No:9, 16080 Osmangazi̇/Bursa, Türkiye
sites.summary: A mostly-Ottoman bathhouse built atop a Byzantine bath that may have hosted Theodora
sites.description: This Ottoman bathhouse was built on top of an ancient Byzantine bath, but records suggest a public bath here as far back as 525 AD, with a tradition that Justinian's wife Theodora bathed here. Marble capitals and columns worked by Byzantine stonemasons.

sites.name: Mausoleum of Saint Helena at Tor Pignattara
alternateNames: Catacombe dei SS. Marcellino e Pietro
sites.summary: Constantinian rotunda used as the mausoleum of St. Helena
sites.description: Built by Constantine beside the basilica of Saints Marcellinus and Peter, as a domed rotunda probably first meant for the emperor, then used for his mother Helena. Her porphyry sarcophagus now resides in the Vatican Museums.

sites.name: Byzantine Museum of Kastoria
sites.summary: A museum with 700 icons from the 12th to the 17th century
sites.description: Atop the Byzantine acropolis, it holds around 700 icons drawn from the city's roughly 75 Byzantine and post-Byzantine churches, dating from the 12th to the 17th century, with about 35 on permanent display.

sites.name: Gortyna Archaeological Site
sites.summary: A site with Byzantine remains from the 6th century until the city faded under Arab raiding and looting
sites.description: Capital of the early Byzantine province. According to Eusebius, Titus was the first bishop of Crete, and the traditional site of his tomb is marked by the Basilica of St. Titus, built in the 6th century under Justinian. The smaller church nearby survived the earthquakes.

sites.name: Vrontisi Monastery
sites.summary: A Byzantine monastery with 14th century frescoes and a 15th century marble fountain
sites.description: Probably founded in the Second Byzantine period, it flourished under the Venetians and declined after 1669. It retains 14th-century frescoes; Michael Damaskinos of the Cretan School is said to have been a monk here.

sites.name: Toplou Monastery
sites.summary: A Venetian-era fortress monastery with Byzantine roots and art
sites.description: This monastery's founding probably dates to the late 14th century, and it took its fortress form after Turkish pirate raids at the end of the 15th, rebuilt by the Venetian-Cretan residents. Holds a notable post-Byzantine icon and 14th century frescoes.

sites.name: Varsamonerou Monastery
sites.summary: A monastery church with notable 14th and 15th century Palaiologan style frescoes
sites.description: Of Byzantine origin, though built in the early period of Venetian domination, the surviving katholikon is a treasury of frescoes by named painters of the Palaiologan tradition from the 14th and 15th centuries.

sites.name: Moni Agiou Georgiou Vrachasioti
sites.summary: This two-aisled church (St. George and St. Demetrios) preserves 14th-century frescoes on the north wall
sites.description: This two-aisled church (St. George and St. Demetrios) preserves 14th-century frescoes on the north wall and a 16th century bell tower.

sites.name: Palianis Monastery
sites.summary: One of the oldest Byzantine churches on the island, with first and second period ruins
sites.description: Founded next to the ancient town of Apollonia, possibly on a temple of Athena, this church is one of the oldest on the island, with reused Byzantine marble columns and capitals; ruins of earlier First- and Second-Byzantine churches survive around it.

sites.name: Faneromenis Monastery
sites.summary: A quiet monastery with a riotous history and fire-blackened medieval frescoes
sites.description: A quiet monastery founded in the 13th century with 15th century frescoes in the katholikon. It suffered badly under Turkish rule and was burned out while serving as a rebel hideout.

sites.name: Monastery of Panagia Faneromeni
sites.address: Τράχηλα Σκοπῆς Σητείας, Panagia Faneromeni 723 00, Greece
sites.summary: A fortress-monastery set in a cave on Mt. Stavros, the katholikon contains fire-blackened frescoes
sites.description: The original church here was probably built in the second Byzantine period, between 1000 and 1200, but much of what is seen today is Venetian. There is a cave-set katholikon with frescoes blackened by fires set by the Ottomans.

sites.name: Church of Agios Antonios
sites.summary: A small, 14th century stone church with connections to hesychasts
sites.description: This little stone church sits at the seaward end of the Gorge of the Saints, built in the 14th century and enlarged into the 15th century. Sea-salt and pirate raids destroyed the murals.

sites.name: Agios Andreas
sites.summary: A modern cathedral over a previous Byzantine structure, home to the skull of St. Andrew
sites.description: While what you will see here today is neo-Byzantine, genuinely old layers are underneath and beside it. Thomas Palaiologos, last despot of the Morea, gifted the skull of St. Andrew to Pope Pius II, and in 1964, Pope Paul VI sent the skull here, back to Patras.

sites.name: Odigìtria Monastery
sites.summary: A large Cretan monastery with a 14th century fabric
sites.description: One of Crete's largest monasteries, founded in the 14th century by the Kallergis family. Built as a fortress with a surviving tower and frescoes.

sites.name: Gonia Monastery
sites.summary: A post-Byzantine monastery with a museum of Byzantine artifacts
sites.description: Coastal monastery whose buildings are certainly post-Byzantine Venetian-Cretan, although tradition holds an earlier foundation. Contains a museum of Byzantine artifacts in its basement.

sites.name: Aretiou Monastery
sites.summary: A post-Byzantine monastery with a school of iconography painting
sites.description: A post-Byzantine fortified monastery, and one of the most important on the island. While Venetian-Cretan, it housed a school of iconography that kept the Byzantine style of painting alive on Crete.

sites.name: Panagia Kera Kardiotissa
sites.summary: A post-Byzantine church with 14th century paintings
sites.description: A post-Byzantine era katholikon preserves wall paintings in the characteristic style of the first decade of the 14th century, allied to the Macedonian school.

sites.name: Monastery of St. George
sites.summary: Perhaps a 10th century Byzantine site, the remaining buildings are much later
sites.description: Tradition and certain written sources attest to an original Byzantine monastery here as early as the 10th century. The "old church" on the site now dates to the 17th. Contains a bullet-scarred icon of St. George.

sites.name: Early Christian Basilica of Poros
sites.summary: Excavations of a 5th century church reveal a finely-worked mosaic floor
sites.description: Built around the 4th–5th century and excavated in 1937 and 1960, this three-aisled basilica is thought to have been the cathedral of ancient Olous, now largely submerged in the Elounda lagoon. Its mosaic floor is among the finest in Crete.

sites.name: Early Christian Basilica of Kastri
sites.summary: Excavations of a 6th century basilica with mosaics and a Roman sarcophagus altar
sites.description: On a pretty promontory stand the remains of a large three-aisled basilica built in the late 5th or early 6th century, its narthex, nave and apse paved with polychrome geometric-and-fish mosaics; the altar is a reused Roman sarcophagus.

sites.name: Church of Saint Nicholas
sites.summary: A rare early Byzantine church on Crete with even rarer aniconic, Iconoclastic decoration
sites.description: This small single-aisled domed church, one of the very few examples of early-Byzantine architecture in Crete, was most probably built before the Arab conquest of 827–828 and gave the town its name. Its earliest fresco layer is aniconic since it was decorated during Iconoclasm. A second, figural layer was added in the 14th century.

sites.name: Holy Church of the Virgin Mary Koubelidiki
sites.summary: A layered Byzantine church, from around the 10th century, with frescoes and a rare Trinity in the dome
sites.description: A small triconch church in the citadel inside the old (Justinian-era) walls, and the only domed church in town. The frescoes are multi-phase: the west-front murals date to the 15th century and the narthex to the 17th. There is a rare depiction of the Holy Trinity in the dome.

sites.name: Panagia Mavriotissa Monastery
sites.summary: An 11th century monastery with paintings inside and out
sites.description: Founded in the 11th century, tradition links it to Alexios I Komnenos and to George Palaiologos's 1083 victory over the Normans; it is a timber-roofed basilica whose interior frescoes are well preserved, with 13th-century paintings on the exterior.

sites.name: Agios Stefanos
sites.summary: An architecturally notable middle Byzantine church with a gynaikonitis
sites.description: One of the two oldest churches in town, this is a three-aisled basilica notable for a rare surviving gynaikonitis (upper women's gallery) and two fresco layers. Architecturally notable.

sites.name: Taxiarches tis Mitropoleos
sites.summary: One of the older churches in town, with a noted funerary portrait
sites.description: One of the two oldest churches in town, this is a timber-roofed basilica that later served as the metropolitan cathedral. ts standout is a mid-13th-century funerary portrait on the exterior of Eirene Asenina Komnene, flanked by the Archangel Michael in ar

sites.name: Agios Athanasios tou Mouzaki
sites.summary: The great late-Palaiologan capstone of Kastoria, with brilliant 14th century painting
sites.description: Built and painted in 1383–1384 by the brothers Stoya and Theodoros of the Albanian Mouzaki, this is regarded as the culmination of Kastoria's brilliant second-half-of-the-14th-century painting, including a Deesis in imperial robes.

sites.name: Agios Georgios tou Vounou
sites.summary: A modest church with notable late-Palaiologan frescoes inside
sites.description: This late-Palaiologan church dates to the second half of the 14th century. The interior carries a rich fresco program featuring scenes of the major feasts, the Passion of Christ, and the martyrdoms of saints and apostles, along with a notable St. Gregory Palamas.

sites.name: Agios Nikolaos tou Kasnitzi
sites.summary: Among the finest frescoes in the city, dating to the 12th century
sites.description: A single-nave basilica with a fresco program of about 1170–1180, its interior among the finest in the city; the donor, magistros Nikephoros Kasnitzis, is portrayed holding a model of the church, his wife alongside.

sites.name: Agioi Anargyroi
sites.summary: A middle Byzantine church with 10th to 12th century frescoes
sites.description: The fabric of this church goes back to the 10th century (fragmentary early frescoes survive in the narthex), with the main program added in the 12th century per its inscriptions. Contains a notable donor portrait.

sites.name: Agia Ekaterini Sinaiton
alternateNames: Μουσείο Αγίας Αικατερίνης της Ιεράς Αρχιεπισκοπής Κρήτης
sites.summary: A church housing a museum of icons and liturgical objects
sites.description: Since 1967 this 16th century church has housed the Archdiocese's museum of icons and liturgical objects, reopened in 2015. Also important for institutional and artistic reasons: the "Cretan School" of icon-painting developed in this milieu, with Michael Damaskinos emerging from here.

sites.name: Holy Church of Saint Matthew Sinaitón
sites.summary: A post-Byzantine church with Cretan-School icons and heirlooms
sites.description: A second Sinaitic metochion, a short walk from Agia Ekaterini. The dependency was built in 1508 over an older Byzantine church, and it now holds Cretan-School icons and heirlooms rescued from St. Catherine's when the Ottomans made it into a mosque.

sites.name: Agios Panteleimonas
sites.summary: A pretty Middle Byzantine church from the 11th century with layered paintings from the 11th to the 13th century
sites.description: A three-aisled domed basilica of the Middle Byzantine period, 11th century, preserving earlier remnants on the south side that suggest it stands over an Early Christian church. The wall paintings survive in three layers dating from the later 11th into the 13th century.

sites.name: Panagia Fodele
sites.summary: A Middle Byzantine church with layered frescoes
sites.description: An 11th-century cruciform church of the early Second Byzantine period, built directly within the nave of a ruined 7th-century Early Christian three-aisled basilica. Two fresco layers survive, revealed when later whitewash was removed. Across the street is a small museum to El Greco.

sites.name: Panagia Kera
sites.summary: A church with the best-preserved Byzantine-era frescoes on the island, dating from the 13th century
sites.description: This church holds the best-preserved Byzantine-era frescoes on Crete and is among the island's most significant churches. It's a Byzantine-style church whose core is dated to the 13th century, built up in phases.

sites.name: Afentis Christos Church
sites.summary: A small church with late-medieval frescoes
sites.description: A small single-nave, barrel-vaulted church of the Transfiguration; the custodian of Gouverniotissa holds the keys here too. The rich surviving frescoes are from the 14th or 15th century.

sites.name: Panagia Gouverniotissa Monastery
sites.address: Επαρχιακή Οδός Ποταμιών - Τζερμιάδων, Gonies 700 05, Greece
sites.summary: One of the oldest Byzantine monasteries on Crete with 14th century frescoes
sites.description: An inscribed cross-in-square katholikon dedicated to the Dormition, with Christ Pantokrator in the central dome and prophets, the Crucifixion and more on the walls. Tradition founds it in the 10th century after the reconquest from the Arabs, making it one of the oldest Byzantine monasteries on Crete.

sites.name: Byzantine and Post-Byzantine Collection of Chania
sites.summary: A Byzantine museum collection in a Venetian church building
sites.description: Housed in a Venetian Franciscan church the holdings are the real Byzantine content: a 6th-century basilica mosaic floor, frescoes such as those from Agia Varvara at Latziana, and an icon of St. George on horseback by Emmanuel Tzanes (1660–1680).

sites.name: Kastelli archaeological site
sites.summary: A layered archaeological site, with a Byzantine fortification layer
sites.description: This low hill is the acropolis of ancient Kydonia, once a Minoan palatial center that yielded Linear B tablets. 6th-century Byzantine walls were raised over the Bronze Age stratigraphy using Kydonia's own stone, and after 1252 the Venetians settled inside those Byzantine walls before expanding downhill.

sites.name: Byzantine Acropolis of Serres
sites.summary: A site in Macedonia containing multiple Byzantine sites
sites.description: The fortified hill north of the city, containing a Byzantine castle first built in the 9th century and linked to Nikephoros Phokas, while most surviving walls and buildings are 14th-century. Also contains the Church of Agios Nikolaos, restored in the 20th century, but attested to as early as the 14th century.

sites.name: Western Walls of Thessaloniki
sites.summary: Four kilometers of genuine Byzantine city walls
sites.description: The surviving circuit dates mainly to around 390, in the early Byzantine period. A major late-4th/early-5th-century reconstruction is credited to the eparch Hormisdas, whose long inscription survives on the western wall, with further Palaiologan repairs.

sites.name: Anna Palaiologina Gate
sites.summary: A Palaiologan gate with a specific marble inscription
sites.description: A precisely dated Palaiologan gate on the upper (acropolis) walls near the Trigonion tower. Its marble inscription records that it was built by order of "the powerful and holy mistress Lady Anna Palaiologina," 1355-56.

sites.name: Agios Minas (Saints Menas, Victor and Vincent)
alternateNames: Ιερός Ναός Αγίων Μηνά, Βίκτωρος και Βικεντίου
sites.summary: A modern church with a few remains of the Byzantine original
sites.description: Very little remains of the original, 5th century church: only the sanctuary niche and a couple of columns and marble members survive, some now in the Museum of Byzantine Culture.

sites.name: Agia Aikaterini
sites.summary: A beautiful 14th century church with Macedonian-School painting
sites.description: A late-13th/early-14th-century church with five domes and an ambulatory, with elaborate brickwork and murals contemporary with construction. A clean Palaiologan example with in-situ Macedonian-school painting.

sites.name: Byzantine Bath
sites.address: Θεοτοκοπούλου, Κρίσπου, Χρυσοστόμου, Φιλοκτήτου &, Thessaloniki 546 34, Greece
sites.summary: A rare piece of secular Byzantine architecture from the 14th century
sites.description: The only surviving Byzantine bath in Greece, completed around 1300. This is a rare piece of secular Byzantine architecture in a corpus that's overwhelmingly churches.

sites.name: Church of Saint Nicholas Orphanos
alternateNames: Ιερός Ναός Αγίου Νικολάου των Ορφανών
sites.summary: A Serbian-tinted Byzantine church from the 14th century
sites.description: A small early-14th-century church, its wall paintings are among the most important early-14th-century ensembles in Thessaloniki, Macedonia and Serbia.

sites.name: Vlatadon Monastery
sites.summary: A still-functioning Byzantine era monastery with an architecturally interesting katholikon
sites.description: The only Byzantine-era monastery in Thessaloniki still functioning, founded in the mid-14th century. The katholikon is an unusual cross-in-square whose dome rests on the sanctuary walls because of the earlier building beneath.

sites.name: Museum of Byzantine Culture
sites.summary: A modern museum with an excellent Byzantine collection
sites.description: A modern, purpose-built museum (opened 1994), widely rated among the best of its kind. It contains mosaics, frescoes, icons, coins, sculpture, and fragments from monuments around the area.

sites.name: Holy Cathedral Church of Hagia Sophia
alternateNames: Καθεδρικός Ναός της του Θεού Σοφίας
sites.summary: A major Byzantine site with art from across the Byzantine centuries
sites.description: The great domed church that long served as Thessaloniki's cathedral. The sanctuary holds aniconic mosaics from the Iconoclast period, and the apse Theotokos was set after Iconoclasm's first end, with monograms of Constantine VI and the Empress Irene. The dome later received the Ascension mosaic.

sites.name: Church of the Holy Apostles
sites.summary: One of the period's finest expressions of art, noted for mosaics and frescoes
sites.description: A Late Byzantine church of the Palaiologan Renaissance, prized for its mosaics and frescoes, which visitors have compared to Chora or Pammakaristos. This makes it, with its refined recessed-brick exterior, one of the finest expressions of the period's Constantinopolitan school outside the capital.

sites.name: Panagia Chalkeon
sites.summary: An architecturally stunning church, built in the 11th century
sites.description: Precisely dated by its lintel inscription to 1028, built as a funerary chapel, the founder's tomb is in an arcosolium in the north wall. Architecturally stunning, with elegant brick blind arches and half-columns showing strong Constantinopolitan influence.

sites.name: Profitis Ilias
sites.summary: A 14th century Palaiologan church, restored in the 20th century
sites.description: A 14th-century Palaiologan church on a hill in Ano Poli, it was built ca. 1360–1370 on the site of a palace destroyed in the 1342 Zealot uprising. Restored 1956–61; its murals influenced later Serbian painting.

sites.name: Early Christian Basilica οf Paleopolis
sites.address: Early Christian Basilica of Paleopolis, Dairpfela 16, Kerkira 491 00, Greece
sites.summary: Fragmentary remains of an early church, repeatedly destroyed and rebuilt
sites.description: First built in the 5th century on the ruins of a Roman odeum, this was an imposing, five-aisled complex with rich decoration. It was destroyed repeatedly by Vandals, Goths, Saracens, Normans, and Turks. All that remains now are fragments of the apse and walls.

sites.name: Church of the Transfiguration of the Savior
sites.summary: A small Middle Byzantine church on an island
sites.description: A small church dated to the 11th or 12th century on an island near town. It stays closed most of the year, but opens on August 6th for the Feast of the Transfiguration. The current fabric of the building reflects later reconstruction.

sites.name: Holy Church of the Holy Apostles Jason and Sosipater
alternateNames: Ιερός Ναός Αγίων Αποστόλων Ιάσονος και Σωσιπάτρου
sites.summary: An 11th century church with fragmentary early paintings and later Cretan master paintings
sites.description: Built in the early 11th century, it is the oldest Christian church in Corfu Town and the most significant Byzantine monument on the island. Fragments of 11th–13th-century frescoes survive, and in the 17th century the church gained icons by the Cretan master Emmanuel Tzanes.

sites.name: Byzantine Museum of Antivouniotissa
sites.summary: A Venetian church housing a museum of paintings by Cretan and Heptanese masters
sites.description: The museum occupies the former church of the Holy Mother of God Antivouniotissa ("facing the mountain"), built in the Venetian era. It houses a collection of some ninety portable icons dating from the 15th to the 19th centuries, mostly post-Byzantine work of the Cretan and early Heptanese schools.

sites.name: Panagia Eleousa
sites.summary: A post-Byzantine single-nave katholikon with a beautiful cycle of 16th century Cretan School frescoes
sites.description: A post-Byzantine single-nave katholikon with a beautiful cycle of 16th century Cretan School frescoes and an 18th century narthex layer.

sites.name: Ioannina Castle
sites.summary: A castle with two parts, dating to the 10th century
sites.description: The Kastro occupies a rocky promontory jutting into Lake Pamvotis, with two citadels shaped in Byzantine times: the northeastern seat of the despot and the southeastern Its Kale, or inner castle. Surviving walls are dated to the 10th-11th centuries.

sites.name: Byzantine Museum of Ioannina
sites.summary: A collection of early-Christian sculpture, icons, coins, and manuscripts from across Epirus
sites.description: Inside Its Kale on the site of Ali Pasha's palace, this collection includes early-Christian sculpture, icons, coins, and manuscripts from across Epirus.

sites.name: Agios Nikolaos Filanthropinon
alternateNames: Holy Monastery of Saint Nicholas Philanthropinon
sites.summary: A domed katholikon here holds three post-Byzantine fresco phases
sites.description: Built in 1291/92 by Michael Philanthropinos, who fled to Ioannina after the Fourth Crusade, this single-nave domed katholikon carries three post-Byzantine fresco phases. Famous for the row of Ancient Greek Sages painted in the narthex.

sites.name: Monastery of Prophet Elijah
alternateNames: Ιερά Μονή Προφήτη Ηλία Νήσου Ιωαννίνων
sites.summary: An originally late-Byzantine church, leveled by Ottomans, now visible mostly as spolia in a much later building
sites.description: Tradition holds that the original church went back to the late Byzantine period, but that building was leveled by the Sultan's troops in 1821–22, during the siege that ended Ali Pasha. The church you see was rebuilt within a few years of that destruction, and it reused architectural members from the older church as spolia.

sites.name: Monastery of Saint Nicholas Stratigopoulos (Diliou)
alternateNames: Μονή Αγίου Νικολάου Στρατηγοπούλου ή Ντίλιου
sites.summary: A 13th century monastery with 15th century frescoes, seldom open to the public
sites.description: Founded in the 13th century by the Stratigopoulos family, another Constantinopolitan clan that arrived in 1204, the atholikon was frescoed in 1542–43 (dated by a narthex inscription) by a painter within the Philanthropinon tradition.

sites.name: Agios Ioannis Prodromos
sites.summary: A post-Byzantine church of the 16th century
sites.description: Built 1506–07 by the brothers Nektarios and Theophanis Apsarades, hieromonks of Byzantine aristocratic descent, and frescoed in the 18th century. Post-Byzantine throughout.

sites.name: Duomo of Cefalù
sites.address: Piazza del Duomo, 10, 90015 Cefalù PA, Italy
sites.summary: A Norman-Byzantine cathedral with masterful mosaics
sites.description: Begun in 1131 by Roger II, architecturally it's Arab-Norman/Romanesque, but its glory is the apse mosaic program, and that is thoroughly Byzantine, especially the colossal Christ Pantokrator in the conch. The apse mosaics were laid by master mosaicists brought from Constantinople.

sites.name: Basilica of Santa Lucia al Sepolcro
alternateNames: Santuario di Santa Lucia al Sepolcro
sites.address: Piazza Santa Lucia, 1, 96100 Siracusa SR, Italy
sites.summary: A Norman church with notable Byzantine frescoes and a Byzantine sepolcro
sites.description: Built over the traditional site of St. Lucy's martyrdom, used into the 8th–9th century and preserving Byzantine-era frescoes, including the Forty Martyrs of Sebaste; the martyr's tomb was enshrined in a Byzantine-style octagonal sepolcro after its 6th rediscovery. Church itself is a Norman rebuild.

sites.name: Cathedral of San Ciriaco
sites.address: Piazzale del Duomo, 9, 60121 Ancona AN, Italy
sites.summary: A later church with Byzantine layers and fragmentary remains
sites.description: The acropolis of Greek Ankón held a temple of Aphrodite, over which a 5th–6th-century early-Christian basilica of St. Lawrence was raised (mosaic-floor fragments survive), and the church took its Greek-cross form around the turn of the 10th–11th century.

sites.name: Sacello di San Vittore in Ciel d'Oro
sites.summary: A small cella memoriae incorporated into the basilica with spectacular gold-ground mosaics
sites.description: A small 4th-century cella memoriae built for the martyr Victor, later absorbed into the Basilica of Sant'Ambrogio. Its dome blazes with 5th-century gold-ground mosaics, giving it its name.

sites.name: Municipal Museum of Icons and Byzantine Tradition
alternateNames: Museo delle Icone e della Tradizione Bizantina
sites.summary: A museum of post-Byzantine Orthodox-tradition works
sites.description: A museum of Greek-Byzantine icons in Italy, built around Archimandrite Paolo Lombardo's collection: icons of the 15th–20th centuries from Russia, Greece, the Balkans and beyond, plus vestments and liturgical books.

sites.name: Church of Santa Maria del Mastro
sites.address: Piazza della Repubblica, 89040 Gerace RC, Italy
sites.summary: Real Byzantine-rite institutional fabric under Norman-and-later remodeling
sites.description: Founded 1083–84 in the Norman era at Gerace, originally a Greek-rite church with an east-facing apse and megalomartyr dedications. Reworked when the diocese shifted from the Greek to the Latin rite around 1480.

sites.name: Santa Ruba
sites.address: SS182, 89853 San Gregorio d'Ippona VV, Italy
sites.summary: Perhaps a 10th century Byzantine church, definitely attached to an Italo-Greek monastery
sites.description: The date here is genuinely unsettled, perhaps 10th century but perhaps 17th. However, it was originally attached to a Basilian (Italo-Greek) monastery.

sites.name: Park of the Rupestrian Churches
sites.summary: A massive site of rock-hewn churches with 8th to 13th century art
sites.description: A massive site with over 150 rock-hewn churches, crypts and hermitages carved into the tufa, many frescoed between the 8th and 13th centuries in a blend of Byzantine ("Greco-Oriental") and Western iconography.  Matera was under Byzantine rule from the 6th–11th centuries, and Basilian monks fleeing Iconoclast persecution.

sites.name: Church of Saint Mary of Idris
sites.address: Via Madonna dell'Idris, 75100 Matera MT, Italy
sites.summary: A church carved into a rock spur with 12th-17th century frescoes
sites.description: Carved into a dramatic rock spur; the linked Monterrone crypt holds frescoes of the 12th–17th century. The name "Idris" most likely derives from the Greek Hodegetria

sites.name: Santa Lucia alle Malve
alternateNames: Chiesa di Santa Lucia alle Malve
sites.summary: An 8th century church with some of the earliest Byzantine painting in Italy
sites.description: An 8th-century foundation, the region's first female Benedictine settlement, with frescoes counted among the earliest Byzantine-style painting in Italy, including a Madonna del Latte (Galaktotrophousa).

sites.name: Madonna delle Virtù and San Nicola dei Greci
sites.address: Via Madonna delle Virtù, 75100 Matera MT, Italy
sites.summary: A rock complex with Italo-Greek frescoes
sites.description: A two-level rock complex on the Gravina; "dei Greci" flags the Italo-Greek monastic association, with frescoes in the crypt.

sites.name: Mausoleum of Galla Placidia
sites.address: Via San Vitale, 17, 48121 Ravenna RA, Italy
sites.summary: Excellent mosaics in an unassuming late-Western Roman building
sites.description: The oldest of the Ravenna group, its plain exterior gives no warning of the interior, where every surface above the marble dado is mosaic on a deep midnight-blue ground.

sites.name: Orthodox Baptistery
sites.summary: The orthodox baptistery with superb 5th century mosaics of the baptism of Christ
sites.description: The octagonal baptistery beside the cathedral, built and decorated with excellent mosaics in the 5th century, featuring the orthodox (non-Arian) take on Christ's baptism: Christ in the Jordan, John baptizing, the river personified as a pagan-style river-god.

sites.name: Arian Baptistery
sites.address: Piazzetta degli Ariani, 48121 Ravenna RA, Italy
sites.summary: The Arian baptistery with wonderful mosaics showing interesting differences from the orthodox counterpart
sites.description: The Arian baptistery, featuring many of the same themes as the Orthodox counterpart, but with notable differences, reflecting differing theologies.

sites.name: Basilica of Sant'Apollinare Nuovo
sites.address: Via di Roma, 53, 48121 Ravenna RA, Italy
sites.summary: An Arian palace church with extensive mosaics showing physical signs of the Arian heresy and its aftermath
sites.description: Built around 500 by Theodoric as the Arian palace church, its nave mosaics are the great survival: the upper registers (Christ's miracles and Passion, prophets and saints) are Theodoric-era work, while the lower registers carry the celebrated processions. Later in the 6th century the mosaics were visibly purged of Gothic content.

sites.name: Oratory of Sant'Andrea
sites.summary: An anti-Arian manifesto in mosaic
sites.description: Built during Theodoric's Arian reign as a private orthodox oratory, it is the only early-Christian archiepiscopal chapel to survive intact, and its whole program is an anti-Arian manifesto.

sites.name: Basilica of San Vitale
sites.address: Via San Vitale, 17, 48121 Ravenna RA, Italy
sites.summary: The jewel of Byzantine Ravenna with the most famous images of the Byzantine world
sites.description: The jewel of Byzantine Ravenna. The octagonal, domed plan echoes Sts. Sergius and Bacchus in Constantinople, and the presbytery mosaics are the most famous images of the Byzantine world: Justinian with his retinue facing Theodora and her court. This is Byzantium's imperial theology made visible in the West.

sites.name: Basilica of Sant'Apollinare in Classe
alternateNames: Basilica of St. Apollinaris in Classe
sites.address: Via Romea Sud, 224, 48124 Classe RA, Italy
sites.summary: A 6th century Justinianic church in Ravenna containing an enormous expanse of apse mosaic
sites.description: Consecrated in 549 by Maximian, in the old naval port of Classe, this church holds one of the largest surviving expanses of ancient apse mosaic: a symbolic Transfiguration over a luminous green paradise where St. Apollinaris stands orant among twelve lambs.

sites.name: Throne of Maximian
sites.summary: Inside the archiepiscopal museum, the 6th century ivory cathedra of Maximian
sites.description: The ivory cathedra of the Archbishop Maximian named in San Vitale's Justinian panel, made in the mid-6th century. It was almost certainly carved in an imperial workshop at Constantinople and sent west.

sites.name: Domus dei Tappeti di Pietra
sites.address: Via Gian Battista Barbiani, 16, 48121 Ravenna RA, Italy
sites.summary: An underground archaeological site with Byzantine era mosaic floors
sites.description: An underground archaeological site with some 700 m² of floor uncovered by chance in 1993 during excavation work. The remains are layered, but the showpiece is a 5th-6th century private residence's floors paved in polychrome tesserae and marble inlay.

sites.name: San Vincenzo al Volturno
sites.address: SS158, Rocchetta a Volturno IS, Italy
sites.summary: An abbey with a crypt with 9th century frescoes
sites.description: This abbey's treasure is the Crypt of Epiphanius (abbot 824–842), a nearly intact 9th-century fresco cycle on a Greek-cross plan, its saints in Byzantine dress, a Christ Pantokrator on a blue globe, and Marian and Passion scenes.

sites.name: Oratory of San Pellegrino
sites.address: Via Antonio de Dominicis, 67020 Bominaco AQ, Italy
sites.summary: A 13th century chapel with Gothic-Byzantine frescoes
sites.description: The "Sistine Chapel of Abruzzo": covered wall-to-wall with a near-complete 13th-century fresco cycle. The idiom is Gothic naturalism grafted onto Benedictine and Byzantine models. Not Byzantine per se, but drawing on the tradition.

sites.name: Cattolica di Stilo
sites.summary: A middle-Byzantine brick church with remains of Byzantine frescoes
sites.description: A small 9th–10th-century brick church of the middle-Byzantine type descended from Constantinople's Church of the Holy Apostles. Contains the remains of Byzantine frescoes and Greek/Arabic inscriptions.

sites.name: San Giovanni Theristis
alternateNames: Monastero Ortodosso di San Giovanni Theristis
sites.address: Contrada San Giovanni, 89040 Bivongi RC, Italy
sites.summary: A Byzantine-Norman monastery church
sites.description: This church is a synthesis of Byzantine and Norman work: Byzantine banded brick-and-stone exterior, Norman piers and arches inside. Revived and now a living Orthodox monastery.

sites.name: Eremo di Santa Maria della Stella
sites.address: 89040 Pazzano, Metropolitan City of Reggio Calabria, Italy
sites.summary: A cave-cut sanctuary with Italo-Byzantine frescoes
sites.description: A sanctuary carved into a cave on Monte Stella, reached by 62 rock-cut steps, originating as an Italo-Greek Basilian hermitage. Surviving Byzantine frescoes include the Trinity, Christ, Archangel Michael, a Pietà, and a St. Mary of Egypt receiving communion from the monk Zosimas.

sites.name: Museum of the Diocese and the Rossano Codex
sites.summary: A museum whose crown jewel is a 6th century Greek Gospel book with purple dyed parchment and gold and silver ink
sites.description: Rossano's Diocesan and Codex Museum holds the Codex Purpureus Rossanensis, a 6th-century Greek Gospel book of purple-dyed parchment written in gold and silver ink, with about fifteen miniatures, carried west by a monk fleeing the Arab conquests or Iconoclasm.

sites.name: Chiesa di Santa Maria del Pàtire
sites.summary: A celebrated 11th century monastery with scriptorium and Greek library
sites.description: Founded around 1095 by St. Bartholomew of Simeri on an earlier Byzantine site. A Latin-Norman basilica plan with a fine cosmatesque-style mosaic floor.

sites.name: Church of San Giovanni Chrysostom
sites.address: Via Duca d'Aosta, 89040 Gerace RC, Italy
sites.summary: A middle-Byzantine stone church built in the 10th-11th century
sites.description: Once the katholikon of a monastery, built in the 10th-11th century, this is a Byzantine church through and through, with an east-facing apse, niches for prothesis and diaconicon, fresco traces, and a rainwater cistern. Now reconsecrated and used as a Greek Orthodox church.

sites.name: La Cattedrale di Maria Santissima di Romania
sites.summary: A 12th century Norman church with a venerated 14th century icon of the Byzantine tradition
sites.description: A 12th-century Norman church, much restored, that houses the venerated icon of the Madonna di Romania ("Romania" being the Byzantines' own name for their empire), dated to the 14th century and credited with sparing the church from WWII bombs, still displayed undetonated by the door.

sites.name: Santuario di Santa Maria dell'Isola
sites.summary: A Norman church that is picture-postcard pretty, but with only a historical connection to the Byzantines
sites.description: This jutting rock over the sea was a retreat for Greek/Eastern hermit monks from around the 7th–8th century, and a church here (variously dated 6th–9th century) belonged to Basilian (Italo-Greek) monks while Calabria still lay under Byzantine rule. The chapter closed with the Normans, and the modern building is later.

sites.name: Basilica di San Marco
sites.address: P.za San Marco, 328, 30100 Venezia VE, Italy
sites.summary: An 11th century church by Greek architects modeled on Holy Apostles of Constantinople and containing massive Byzantine-style mosaics and notable art stolen from Constantinople itself
sites.description: Begun in 1063, this cathedral's declared model was the sixth-century Church of the Holy Apostles in Constantinople and was built by Greek architects. Following the sack of Constantinople in 1204, the façades were richly decorated with spolia and remains the largest surviving repository of plundered Byzantine art in the West. Its gold-ground mosaics consciously follow middle-Byzantine iconographic programs.

sites.name: Cattedrale di Santa Maria Assunta
sites.address: Via isola, Campiello Lazzari, di, 30142 campello VE, Italy
sites.summary: The oldest building in the lagoon with monumental mosaics, including a Greek-inscribed Hodegetria in the apse and a Last Judgment on the western wall
sites.description: The oldest building in the lagoon, founded by the Exarch Isaac of Ravenna in 639, reconstructed in 1008. Its fame rests on remarkable Veneto-Byzantine mosaics: in the apse a standing Virgin and Child on gold, a Hodegetria labeled in Greek, and especially a monumental Last Judgement filling the whole west wall, originally eleventh-century.

sites.name: Chiesa di Santa Fosca
sites.address: Fondamenta dei Borgognoni, 24, 30142 Venezia VE, Italy
sites.summary: A small martyrion adjoining the cathedral; Byzantine-idiom architecture rather than an eastern foundation
sites.description: Adjoining the cathedral, Santa Fosca was rebuilt in the 11th–12th century as a martyrion. It is a compact, central plan Venetian-Byzantine church.

sites.name: Cathedral Basilica of Saints Mary and Donato
alternateNames: Basilica dei Santi Maria e Donato
sites.address: Campo S. Donato, 11, 30141 Venezia VE, Italy
sites.summary: A Veneto-Byzantine church with a glorious mosaic floor and a gold apse Madonna
sites.description: Built on a 7th-century foundation but completely rebuilt between 1125 and 1141 in a Veneto-Byzantine style, its glory is the pavement: a famed 12th-century Veneto-Byzantine mosaic floor, over 500 square meters of porphyry, serpentine, and other stones mixed with glass paste, in Byzantine-Roman opus sectile. The apse holds a Madonna Orante on gold.

sites.name: Basilica di Sant'Eufemia
sites.address: Campo Patriarca Elia, 13, 34073 Grado GO, Italy
sites.summary: A 6th century Byzantine-era church with well-preserved mosaics
sites.description: Consecrated in 579, this basilica was the seat of the pro-Roman and pro-Byzantine branch of the church. Its fame comes from exceptionally well-preserved sixth-century floor mosaics plus an octagonal baptistery with its own 6th-century mosaics.

sites.name: City Wall of Durrës
sites.address: Muri Kalase, Rruga Kalase, Durrës, Albania
sites.summary: A well-preserved Byzantine wall
sites.description: The defensive circuit around the old city, built by Anastasius I, and one of the best-preserved such systems in Albania.

sites.name: Dürres Amphitheater
sites.summary: A Roman amphitheater with a Byzantine chapel and mosaics inside
sites.description: While this is undoubtedly an Imperial Roman amphitheater, started under Trajan, the Byzantinist will find a 4th century chapel inside of it, originally decorated with frescoes, now with 6th century Early Christian Mosaics. A medieval chapel was built in the 13th century.

sites.name: Byzantine Forum
sites.summary: The Byzantine-era forum of Durrës
sites.description: A circular archaeological site representing the urban core of Byzantine Dyrrachium, and containing a colonnade, ancient baths, and market ruins.

sites.name: Auditorium Santa Lucia
sites.summary: A Romanesque church, now concert hall, with 8th to 11th century roots
sites.description: Deconsecrated in 1972, this 11th century church replaced an earlier church of the 8th or 9th century. It's Romanesque, with Early Christian and Byzantine influences, and now operates as a concert hall.

sites.name: Cathedral of St John the Baptist
alternateNames: Church of St John the Precursor
sites.summary: A genuine Byzantine church with signature candy-striped masonry
sites.description: Built in the Byzantine style during the Khazar era in the 8th century, and one of the oldest churches in Eastern Europe, the alternating white stone and red brick masonry is its signature.

sites.name: Church of the Holy Apostles Peter and Paul
alternateNames: Црква Светих апостола Петра и Павла у Расу
sites.summary: A UNESCO-listed Byzantine church in the former medieval capital of Serbia
sites.description: The oldest intact church in Serbia, early Byzantine in style, completed around 820. It was raised on the remains of an early-Christian church of the 7th century, the site itself layered with Roman and Iron-Age material. Frescoes date from the early 10th century onward, and it is now UNESCO-listed.

sites.name: Church of the Theotokos
alternateNames: Church of the Dormition of the Virgin
sites.summary: One of Albania's oldest churches, tied by legend to Justinian and a relic of the True Cross
sites.description: A domed cross-in-square church in a village of the Drino valley in southern Albania, and one of the oldest in the country. Local tradition credits its founding to Justinian, who is said to have sent a fragment of the True Cross that gave the village its name ('of the Cross'); the building you see is later Byzantine work.

sites.name: Theodosian Land Walls
sites.address: Sur, Fatih, İstanbul (Golden Horn to the Marmara)
sites.summary: The fifth-century walls that kept Constantinople all but unconquerable for a thousand years
sites.description: The great triple line of land fortifications that sealed off the western approach to Constantinople, thrown up under Theodosius II in the early fifth century. They held for a thousand years, and they're still hugely impressive to walk along even where they've crumbled.

sites.name: Blachernai Palace
sites.summary: The Komnenian and Palaiologan emperors' main residence, in the city's northwest corner
sites.description: The imperial palace up in the northwest corner by the walls, which took over from the Great Palace as the emperors' main residence from the twelfth century. Little survives above ground, but the setting against the walls is evocative.

sites.name: Prison of Anemas
sites.summary: A grim tower in the Blachernai walls where fallen emperors were shut away
sites.description: A hulking tower and substructure set into the Blachernai walls, used to lock up out-of-favor emperors and princes. You can still climb through parts of it.
